compilation.description_en: The Book of Faith of Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā Ibn Abī ʿUmar al-ʿAdanī (d. 243 AH), who taught in Mecca: a short book of reports on faith, its pillars and its conditions, with a chapter heading over nearly every report.

notes.label: Structure
notes.text: A short book in chapters (bāb). Most chapters hold one or two reports; each chapter heading is a chapter here, with its reports under it.

notes.label: English translation
notes.text: The English is the supplied translation, which follows the source record by record. Notes that the translation attaches to a report appear beneath it, apart from the Arabic and English text.

notes.label: Arabic text
notes.text: The Arabic is the text of the source page records, shown as supplied. A report’s printed number stands in its label instead of the text, and page markers are carried over from the source.

notes.label: Isnad and matn
notes.text: The English chain and words are divided as the translation gives them. The Arabic is divided at the same point by a fixed rule that does not alter the text; where the rule finds no clean division, the Arabic is shown whole.

notes.label: Transmitters
notes.text: Transmission paths list the names the translation gives for each chain, in English only. No transmitter is identified beyond the wording of the source.

notes.label: Dating
notes.text: The date shown is the death year of Ibn Abī ʿUmar al-ʿAdanī, 243 AH, not a verified date of composition.

notes.label: Coverage
notes.text: 79 entries in 56 sections, in the source order.

groups.title_en: Chapter on fighting over each pillar of the pillars of Islam
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ فِي الْقِتَالِ عَلَى كُلِّ رُكْنٍ مِنْ أَرْكانِ الْإِسْلَامِ

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو الْفَرَجِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُمَرَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يُونُسَ الْجَصَّاصُ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو عَلِيٍّ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ الصَّوَّافُ قِرَاءَةً عَلَيْهِ وَأَنَا أَسْمَعُ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ هَارُونَ بْنِ يُوسُفَ بْنِ هَارُونَ بْنِ زِيَادٍ. قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنَا أَسْمَعُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي عُمَرَ الْمَكِّيُّ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ وَهْبٍ الْمِصْرِيُّ، عَنْ أُسَامَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ حَنْظَلَةَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ الْأَسْلَمِيِّ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: بَعَثَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ خَالِدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ " وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ عَلَى خَمْسٍ فَمَنْ تَرَكَ وَاحِدَةً مِنْهُنَّ قَاتَلَهُ عَلَيْهَا كَما يُقَاتِلُهُ عَلَى الْخَمْسِ عَلَى: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَصَوْمِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ "
records.isnad_en: Abū al-Faraj Muḥammad b. ʿUmar b. Muḥammad b. Yūnus al-Jaṣṣāṣ informed us. He said: Abū ʿAlī Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. al-Ḥasan b. Isḥāq al-Ṣawwāf informed us, by reading to him while I was listening. He said: Abū Aḥmad Hārūn b. Yūsuf b. Hārūn b. Ziyād informed us, it being read to him while I was listening. He said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā b. Abī ʿUmar al-Makkī narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh b. Wahb al-Miṣrī informed us, from Usāma b. Zayd. He said: Ibn Shihāb narrated to me, from Ḥanẓala b. ʿAlī al-Aslamī. He said:
records.matn_en: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq sent Khālid b. al-Walīd and commanded him to fight the people over five: whoever abandons one of them, he is to fight him over it just as he fights him over the five—over the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakāt, the fast of the month of Ramaḍān, and the pilgrimage to the House.

narrators.en: Abū al-Faraj Muḥammad b. ʿUmar al-Jaṣṣāṣ
Abū ʿAlī Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-Ṣawwāf
Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā b. Abī ʿUmar (al-ʿAdanī) al-Makkī

translator_notes: This narration gives the full transmission frame (al-Jaṣṣāṣ ← al-Ṣawwāf ← Hārūn b. Yūsuf ← Ibn Abī ʿUmar); the later narrations give only an abbreviated frame (‘Muḥammad informed us. Abū Aḥmad informed us…’), the earlier links being understood. The source places an opening quotation mark immediately after Khālid’s name, before ‘and he commanded him’.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Prayer is part of faith

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ وَهْبٍ الْمِصْرِيُّ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْحَارِثِ، عَنْ دَرَّاجِ أَبِي السَّمْحِ، عَنْ أَبِي الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: " إِذَا رَأَيْتُمُ الرَّجُلَ يَتَعَاهَدُ الْمَسْجِدَ فَاشْهَدُوا لَهُ بِالْإِيمَانِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: {إِنَّمَا يَعْمُرُ مَسَاجِدَ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ} [التوبة: 18] الْآيَةَ
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd Allāh b. Wahb al-Miṣrī narrated to us, from ʿAmr b. al-Ḥārith, from Darrāj Abū al-Samḥ, from Abū al-Haytham, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: When you see a man who frequents the mosque, bear witness for him to faith. God Almighty said: “Only he shall maintain God’s mosques who believes in God” [Q. 9:18]—the verse.
translator_notes: The numbering passes from 1 to 3 here; no. 2 is not present in this export. The source gives an opening quotation mark before ‘When you see’ but no closing one; ‘the verse’ (al-āya) indicates that the citation is abbreviated.

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ الدَّرَاوَرْدِيُّ، عَنْ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ كَعْبِ الْأَحْبَارِ، قَالَ: قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: " اخْتَارَ اللَّهُ الْبِلَادَ ⦗ص: 69⦘ ، فَأَحَبُّ الْبِلَادِ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى الْبَلَدُ الْحَرَامُ، وَاخْتَارَ اللَّهُ الشُّهُورَ، فَأَحَبُّ الشُّهُورِ إِلَى اللَّهِ الشَّهْرُ الْحَرَامُ، وَأَحَبُّ هَذِهِ الْأشْهُرِ إِلَى اللَّهِ ذُو الْحِجَّةِ، وَأَحَبُّ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ إِلَيْهِ الْعَشْرُ الْأُولَى، وَاخْتَارَ الْأَيَّامَ، فَأَحَبُّ الْأَيَّامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ، وَاخْتَارَ اللَّيَالِيَ، فَأَحَبُّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى اللَّهِ لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ، وَاخْتَارَ السَّاعَاتِ، فَأَحَبُّ السَّاعاتِ إِلَى اللَّهِ سَاعاتُ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْمَكْتُوبَاتِ، وَاخْتَارَ الْكَلَامَ، فَأَحَبُّ الْكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ للَّهِ، فَمَنْ قَالَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ فَهِيَ كَلِمَةُ الْإِخْلَاصِ، كُتِبَ لَهُ عِشْرُونَ حَسَنَةً وَمُحِيَ عَنْهُ عِشْرُونَ سَيِّئَةً، وَمَنْ قَالَ: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، كُتِبَ لَهُ عِشْرُونَ حَسَنَةً وَمُحِيَ عَنْهُ عِشْرُونَ سَيِّئَةً، وَمَنْ قَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَّا خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ وَاسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ سَبَّحَهُ، وَمَنْ قَالَ: الْحَمْدُ للَّهِ، كُتِبَ لَهُ ثَلَاثُونَ حَسَنَةً وَمُحِيَ عَنْهُ ثَلَاثُونَ سَيِّئَةً، وَمَنْ أَقَامَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَآتَى الزَّكَاةَ، وَصَامَ رَمَضَانَ، وَأَحَبَّ لِلَّهِ، وَأَبْغَضَ لِلَّهِ، وَأَعْطَى لِلَّهِ، وَمَنَعَ لِلَّهِ فَقَدِ اسْتَكْمَلَ الْإِيمَانَ "
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Darāwardī narrated to us, from Suhayl b. Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, who said: He said:
records.matn_en: “God chose the lands [p. 69], and the most beloved of lands to God is the Sacred Land (al-balad al-ḥarām); and God chose the months, and the most beloved of months to God is the sacred month (al-shahr al-ḥarām); and the most beloved of these months to God is Dhū al-Ḥijja, and the most beloved part of Dhū al-Ḥijja to Him is the first ten days; and He chose the days, and the most beloved of days to God is the day of Friday; and He chose the nights, and the most beloved night to God is the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr); and He chose the hours, and the most beloved of hours to God are the hours of the prescribed prayers; and He chose speech, and the most beloved speech to God is: There is no god but God, God is greatest, Glory be to God, and Praise be to God. Whoever says ‘There is no god but God’—it is the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlāṣ)—twenty good deeds are written for him and twenty evil deeds are wiped away from him; and whoever says ‘God is greatest’, twenty good deeds are written for him and twenty evil deeds are wiped away from him; and whoever says ‘Glory be to God’—for God, when He created everything and rose over the Throne, glorified Him; and whoever says ‘Praise be to God’, thirty good deeds are written for him and thirty evil deeds are wiped away from him; and whoever establishes the prayer, gives the zakāt, fasts Ramaḍān, loves for God’s sake, hates for God’s sake, gives for God’s sake and withholds for God’s sake has perfected faith.”
translator_notes: No number is printed in the source for this narration; it follows no. 3 and precedes no. 4. It is a saying of Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, not a report from the Prophet; the doubled ‘He said: He said’ is as printed. The clause on ‘Glory be to God’ is elliptical in the source: no reward is stated for it and the subject of ‘glorified Him’ is unclear; the rendering is literal.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Severity regarding staying away from the Friday prayer
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ التَّشْديدُ فِي التَّخَلُّفِ عَنِ الْجُمُعَةِ

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ ثَوْبَانَ، رَفَعَ الْحَدِيثَ قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «مَنْ سَمِعَ الْأَذَانَ ثَلَاثَ جُمُعاتٍ، ولَمْ يَحْضُرَ الْجُمُعَةَ، كُتِبَ مِنَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ»
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us. He said: Maʿmar informed us, from Yaḥyā b. Abī Kathīr, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Thawbān, who raised the ḥadīth, saying:
records.matn_en: “Whoever hears the call to prayer on three Fridays and does not attend the Friday prayer is written among the hypocrites.”

narrators.en: Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Thawbān

translator_notes: Ibn Thawbān ‘raised’ the report (rafaʿa al-ḥadīth) without naming a Companion or the Prophet; the source does not state to whom it is raised.

groups.title_en: Chapter on abandoning disputation (al-mirāʾ)

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْحَكَمِ مَرْوَانُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْوَاحِدِ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ أَبِي دَرِمٍ، عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: بُلِّغَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبَّاسٍ عَنْ مَجْلِسٍ كَانَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ، فِي نَاحِيَةِ بَابِ بَنِي سَهْمٍ يَجْلِسُ فِيهِ نَاسٌ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، فَيَجْتَمِعونَ فَتَرْتَفِعُ أَصْواتُهُمْ، فقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: «انْطَلِقْ بِنا إِلَيْهِمْ» ، فانْطَلَقْنا إِلَيْهِمْ حَتَّى وَقَفْنا عَلَيْهِمْ، فقَالَ لِي ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: «أَخْبِرْهُمْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الَّذِي كَلَّمَ بِهِ الْفَتَى أَيُّوبَ عليه السلام وَهُوَ فِي مَلَأِهِ» ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: قَالَ الْفَتَى ⦗ص: 72⦘ : يَا أَيُّوبُ مَا كَانَ فِي عَظَمَةِ اللَّهِ، وَذِكْرُ الْمَوْتِ مَا يُكِلُّ لِسَانَكَ، وَيَقْطَعُ قَلْبَكَ، وَيَكْسِرُ حُجَّتَكَ؟ يَا أَيُّوبُ، أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ للَّهِ عِبَادًا أَسْكَتَتْهُمْ خَشْيَةُ اللَّهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِيٍّ وَلَا بَكَمٍ، وَأَنَّهُمْ لَهُمُ النُّبَلَاءُ الطُّلَقَاءُ الْفُصَحَاءُ الْأَلِبَّاءُ الْعَالِمُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَأَيَّامِهِ، وَلَكِنَّهُمْ إِذَا ذَكَرُوا عَظَمَةَ الْمَوْتِ، تَقَطَّعَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ، وَكَلَّتْ أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ، وَطَاشَتْ عُقُولُهُمْ وَأَحْلَامُهُمْ فَرَقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهَيْبَةً لَهُ، فَإِذَا اسْتَفَاقُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ اسْتَبَقُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ بِالْأَعْمَالِ الزَّاكِيَةِ، لَا يسَتَكْثِرُونَ للَّهِ الْكَثِيرَ وَلَا يَرْضُونَ لَهُ بِالْقَليلِ، وَيَعُدُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ مَعَ الظَّالِمِينَ وَالْخَاطِئِينَ، وَإِنَّهُمْ لَأَنْزَاهٌ أَبْرَارٌ وَمَعَ الْمُضَيِّعِينَ وَالْمُفَرِّطِينَ، وَإِنَّهُمْ لَأَكْيَاسٌ أَقْوِيَاءُ، نَاحِلُونَ دَائِبُونَ يَرَاهُمُ الْجَاهِلُ فَيَقُولُ مَرْضَى وَلَيْسُوا بَمَرْضَى، وَقَدْ خُولِطُوا وَقَدْ خَالَطَ الْقَوْمَ أَمْرٌ عَظِيمٌ " قَالَ أَبُو الْحَكَمِ: وَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ رَجُلٌ، أَنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ لَهُمْ عَلَى أَثَرِ هَذَا الْكَلَامِ: «كَفى بِكَ ظَالِمًا أَنْ لَا تَزَالَ مُخَاصِمًا، وَكَفَى بِكَ إِثْمًا أَنْ لَا تَزَالَ مُمَارِيًا، وَكَفَى بِكَ كَاذِبًا أَنْ لَا تَزَالَ مُحَدِّثًا بِغَيْرِ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ»
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Abū al-Ḥakam Marwān b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us. He said: Mūsā b. Abī Darim narrated to us, from Wahb b. Munabbih, who said:
records.matn_en: Word reached ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās about a gathering in the Sacred Mosque, in the area of the Gate of Banū Sahm, where people of Quraysh would sit and gather and their voices would rise. Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Come with us to them.” So we went to them until we stood over them, and Ibn ʿAbbās said to me: “Tell them of the words with which the youth spoke to Job (a) while he was among his company.” He said: I said: The youth said [p. 72]: O Job, was there not in the greatness of God, and the mention of death, what would wear out your tongue, cut your heart, and break your argument? O Job, do you not know that God has servants whom the fear of God has silenced, without any impediment or muteness? They are the noble ones, the free-spoken, the eloquent, the intelligent, who know God and His days. But when they remember the greatness of death, their hearts are cut, their tongues wear out, and their minds and wits are scattered in dread of God and awe of Him; and when they recover from that they race to God with pure deeds. They do not think the much they do for God to be much, nor are they content with the little for Him; and they count themselves among the wrongdoers and the sinners, though they are in truth the pure and the righteous, and among the neglectful and the negligent, though they are in truth the shrewd and the strong. They are lean and tireless; the ignorant sees them and says: They are sick—and they are not sick; they have been afflicted (khūliṭū), and a mighty matter has mingled with the people. Abū al-Ḥakam said: A man wrote to me that Ibn ʿAbbās said to them following these words: “It is enough to make you a wrongdoer that you never cease to quarrel, enough to make you a sinner that you never cease to dispute (mumārī), and enough to make you a liar that you never cease to talk about anything other than the remembrance of God.”

narrators.en: Abū al-Ḥakam Marwān b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid

translator_notes: The unnamed ‘me’ is the person to whom Ibn ʿAbbās speaks; the source does not identify him beyond the link to Wahb b. Munabbih. The source has a closing quotation mark after the youth’s speech but no corresponding opening mark. The sense of ‘khūliṭū’ (lit. ‘they have been mingled/confused’) is uncertain and the rendering is tentative. The final lines are Ibn ʿAbbās’s comment, reported by Abū al-Ḥakam from an unnamed man who wrote to him.

groups.title_en: Chapter on that upon which Islam is built

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْمُقْرِئُ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا الْمَسْعُودِيُّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: " أَتَانِي آتٍ، فقَالَ: مَا يَمْنَعُكَ أَنْ تُجَاهِدَ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ، فقَالَ: يَا ابْنَ أَخِي، إِنَّ الْإِسْلَامَ بُنِيَ عَلَى خَمْسٍ، عَلَى شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ، وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ، فَجَعَلَ الرَّجُلُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَقُولَ: وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ، فَيَأْبَى عَلَيْهِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَقُولَ: حَجِّ الْبَيْتِ وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ، وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ الصَّالِحِ، الصِّدْقَ، وَالْجِهَادَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ عز وجل "
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ narrated to us. He said: al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik b. ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar, who said:
records.matn_en: “Someone came to me and said: What prevents you from fighting in jihad, O ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar? He said: O son of my brother, Islam is built on five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakāt, the pilgrimage to the House, and the fast of Ramaḍān. The man wanted to say: the fast of Ramaḍān and the pilgrimage to the House, but ʿAbd Allāh refused him unless he said: the pilgrimage to the House and the fast of Ramaḍān. And among righteous works are truthfulness and jihad in the path of God, mighty and majestic.”
translator_notes: Here the pilgrimage is placed before the fast of Ramaḍān, and ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar insists on that order; the man who corrects him is unnamed.

groups.title_en: Chapter on the attributes of the hypocrites

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ حَدَّثَنَا الْمُقْرِئُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي زِيَادُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: " ثَلَاثٌ أَيُّ مُسْلِمٍ كَانَتْ فِيهِ وَاحِدَةٌ مِنْهُنَّ فَشُعْبَةٌ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ، فَإِنْ كَانَتِ اثْنَتَانِ فَشُعْبَتَانِ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ، فَإِنْ كُنَّ ثَلَاثٌ فَقَدْ أُدْمِجَ بِالْإِيمَانِ مِنْ شَعْرِ رَأْسِهِ إِلَى ظُفُرِ قَدَمِهِ، مَنْ إِذَا قَالَ صَدَقَ، وَإِذَا ائْتُمِنَ أَدَّى، وَإِذَا عَاهَدَ وَفَّى، وَثَلَاثٌ مَنْ كَانَتْ فِيهِ وَاحِدَةٌ مِنْهُنَّ فَشُعْبَةٌ مِنَ النِّفَاقِ، وَإِنْ كَانَتِ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَشُعْبَتَانِ مِنَ النِّفَاقِ، وَإِنْ كُنَّ ثَلَاثٌ فَقَدْ أُدْمِجَ بِالنِّفَاقِ مِنْ شَعْرِ رَأْسِهِ إِلَى ظُفُرِ قَدَمِهِ: مَنْ إِذَا قَالَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا ائْتُمِنَ خَانَ، وَإِذَا عَاهَدَ لَمْ يَفِ "
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. al-Muqriʾ narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Ziyād narrated to us. He said: Ziyād b. Muslim narrated to me, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Three: any Muslim in whom one of them is found has a branch (shuʿba) of faith; if there are two, two branches of faith; and if there are all three, he has been fully enfolded in faith from the hair of his head to the nail of his foot: whoever, when he speaks, speaks truthfully; when entrusted, fulfils the trust; and when he makes a covenant, fulfils it. And three: whoever has one of them has a branch of hypocrisy; if there are two, two branches of hypocrisy; and if there are all three, he has been fully enfolded in hypocrisy from the hair of his head to the nail of his foot: whoever, when he speaks, lies; when entrusted, betrays; and when he makes a covenant, does not fulfil it.”
translator_notes: Mursal: Ziyād b. Muslim does not name a Companion.

groups.title_en: Chapter on the conditions for the perfection of faith

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ أَبِي رَوَّادٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ كَعْبٍ،
records.matn_ar: يَقُولُ فِي قَوْلِهِ {وَالْعَصْرِ} [العصر: 1] «أَقْسَمَ بِهِ رَبُّنَا» . {إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ} [العصر: 2] قَالَ: «النَّاسُ كُلُّهُمْ، ثُمَّ اسْتَثْنَى» ⦗ص: 76⦘ ، فقَالَ {إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ} [العصر: 3] «ثُمَّ لَمْ يَدَعْهُنَّ، وَذَاكَ حَتَّى» قَالَ: {وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ} [العصر: 3] «ثُمَّ لَمْ يَدَعْهُنَّ وَذَاكَ، حَتَّى» قَالَ: {وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ} [العصر: 3] «شُرُوطٌ يُشْتَرَطُ عَلَيْهِمْ»
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Abī Rawwād informed us. He said: I heard Muḥammad b. Kaʿb say, regarding His saying:
records.matn_en: “By the afternoon (al-ʿaṣr)” [Q. 103:1]: “Our Lord has sworn by it.” “Indeed, mankind is in loss” [Q. 103:2]: He said: “All people; then He made an exception” [p. 76], and said: “except those who believe and do righteous deeds” [Q. 103:3]: “then they do not abandon them, and that is until” He said: “and enjoin one another to truth” [Q. 103:3]: “then they do not abandon them, and that is until” He said: “and enjoin one another to patience” [Q. 103:3]: “conditions that are stipulated upon them.”
translator_notes: No number is printed in the source. This is Muḥammad b. Kaʿb’s comment on Sūrat al-ʿAṣr, not a report from the Prophet. The source cites Q. 103:3 for all three clauses.

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي نَجِيحٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ عِكْرِمَةَ مَوْلَى ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: " لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ {وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ} [آل عمران: 85] : قَالَتْ الْيَهُودُ: فَنَحْنُ مُسْلِمُونَ، فَقَالَ اللَّهُ عز وجل لِنَبِيِّهِ: " فَحُجَّهُمْ يَقُولُ: أَخْصِمْهُمْ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عز وجل {وَللَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا وَمَنْ كَفَرَ} [آل عمران: 97] مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمِلَلِ {فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ} [آل عمران: 97] ، فقَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لِنَبِيِّهِ: قُلْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ فَرَضَ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ حَجَّ الْبَيْتِ، فَأَبَوْا وقَالُوا: لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا حَجٌّ "
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, that he heard ʿIkrima, the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbās, say:
records.matn_en: “When {Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers} [Q. 3:85] was revealed, the Jews said: We are Muslims. So God, mighty and majestic, said to His Prophet: ‘Then dispute with them’—he says: overcome them in argument—so God, mighty and majestic, revealed {And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind, for whoever is able to find a way to it; and whoever disbelieves} [Q. 3:97]—from among the people of the religions—{then indeed God is free of need of the worlds} [Q. 3:97]. Then God Almighty said to His Prophet: ‘Say to them: God has made the pilgrimage to the House obligatory upon the Muslims.’ But they refused and said: Pilgrimage is not obligatory upon us.”
translator_notes: No number is printed in the source. ‘Sufyān’ is presumably Sufyān b. ʿUyayna, the shaykh named in the following narrations. The glosses ‘he says: overcome them in argument’ and ‘from among the people of the religions’ are part of the report.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The obligations of Islam and its shares (sihām)

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْمُقْرِئُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْمَسْعُودِيُّ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: " ثَلَاثٌ أَحْلِفُ عَلَيْهِنَّ، وَالرَّابِعَةُ لَوْ حَلَفْتُ عَلَيْهَا لَرَجَوْتُ أَنْ لَا آثَمَ: لَا يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ ذَا سَهْمٍ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ كَمَنْ لَا سَهْمَ لَهُ. وَأسْهَمُ الْإِسْلَامِ: الصَّلَاةُ، وَالزَّكَاةُ، وَالصِّيَامُ، وَلَا يُحِبُّ رَجُلٌ قَوْمًا إِلَّا بَعَثَهُ اللَّهُ مَعَهُمْ، وَلَا يَتَوَلَّى اللَّهُ عز وجل عَبْدًا فِي الدُّنْيَا فَيُوَلِّيهِ سِوَاهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَالرَّابِعَةُ لَوْ حَلَفْتُ عَلَيْهَا لَرَجَوْتُ أَنْ لَا آثَمَ: لَا سَتَرَ اللَّهُ عَلَى عَبْدٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا رَجَوْتُ أَنْ يَسْتُرَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرَةِ "
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: al-Muqriʾ narrated to us. He said: al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Qāsim, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said:
records.matn_en: “Three things I swear to, and as for the fourth, were I to swear to it I would hope not to be sinful: God will not make one who has a share in Islam like one who has no share—and the shares of Islam are prayer, zakāt and fasting; a man does not love a people but God will raise him with them; and God, mighty and majestic, does not take a servant as His ally in this world and then hand him over to another on the Day of Resurrection. And the fourth, were I to swear to it I would hope not to be sinful: God does not conceal [the faults of] a servant in this world but I hope that He will conceal [them] for him in the Hereafter.”
translator_notes: No number is printed in the source; the numbers 8–10 are not present in this export (the next printed number is 11). ‘ʿAbd Allāh’ is presumably Ibn Masʿūd (al-Qāsim being his grandson), but the source gives only ‘ʿAbd Allāh’.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The application of the term ‘disbelief’ to one who abandons prayer
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ إِطْلَاقُ الْكُفْرِ عَلَى مَنْ تَرَكَ الصَّلَاةَ

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْمُقْرِئُ، عَنِ ⦗ص: 78⦘ الْمَسْعُودِيِّ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: «الْكُفْرُ تَرْكُ الصَّلَاةِ»
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, from [p. 78] al-Masʿūdī, from al-Qāsim, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said:
records.matn_en: “Disbelief is abandoning prayer.”
translator_notes: The record is labelled p. 76 in the export, but the marker [p. 78] appears inside it; page 77 is not marked.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The inseparability of works from faith

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا حَكَّامُ بْنُ سَلْمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سِنَانٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ مُرَّةَ الْجَمَليِّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: «الْإِيمَانُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْعَمَلُ قَرِينَانِ لَا يَصْلُحُ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمَا إِلَّا مَعَ صَاحِبِهِ»
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Ḥakkām b. Salm narrated to us, from Abū Sinān, from ʿAmr b. Murra al-Jamalī, from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Faith in God and works are twin companions; neither of them is sound except with its companion.”
translator_notes: Mursal: Muḥammad b. ʿAlī does not name a Companion.

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الدَّرَاوَرْدِيُّ، عَنْ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ كَعْبِ الْأَحْبَارِ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «وَمَنْ أَقَامَ الصَّلَاةَ، وآتَى الزَّكَاةَ، وَصَامَ رَمَضَانَ، وَأَحَبَّ لِلَّهِ، وَأَبْغَضَ لِلَّهِ، وَأَعْطَى لِلَّهِ، وَمَنَعَ لِلَّهِ، فَقَدِ اسْتَكْمَلَ الْإِيمَانَ»
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Muḥammad al-Darāwardī narrated to us, from Suhayl b. Abī Ṣāliḥ, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, who said:
records.matn_en: “Whoever establishes the prayer, gives the zakāt, fasts Ramaḍān, loves for God’s sake, hates for God’s sake, gives for God’s sake and withholds for God’s sake has perfected faith.”
translator_notes: This is the closing sentence of the longer saying of Kaʿb given in the unnumbered narration after no. 3 (p. 69); here Suhayl’s father is omitted from the chain.

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ عِيسَى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْأَعْمَشُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي عَدِيُّ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ زِرِّ بْنِ حُبَيْشٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: عَهِدَ إِلَيَّ النَّبِيُّ عليه السلام أَنَّهُ «لَا يُحِبُّكَ إِلَّا مُؤْمِنٌ، وَلَا ⦗ص: 81⦘ يُبْغِضُكَ إِلَّا مُنَافِقٌ»
records.isnad_en: Muḥammad informed us. He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā narrated to us. He said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us. He said: ʿAdī b. Thābit narrated to me, from Zirr b. Ḥubaysh, from ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, who said:
records.matn_en: The Prophet (a) made a covenant with me that “none loves you but a believer, and none [p. 81] hates you but a hypocrite.”
translator_notes: The honorific (a) after ‘the Prophet’ is as printed in the source.

groups.title_en: Chapter on divine decree (al-qadar)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ عِيسَى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ تَمِيمِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: «لَا يَجِدُ عَبْدٌ طَعْمَ الْإِيمَانِ حَتَّى يَعْلَمَ أَنَّ مَا أَخْطَأَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُصِيبَهُ، وَأَنَّ مَا أَصَابَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَهُ»
records.isnad_en: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā narrated to us. He said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Tamīm b. Salama, from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: ʿAbd Allāh said:
records.matn_en: “A servant does not taste the sweetness of faith until he knows that what missed him was never going to befall him, and that what befell him was never going to miss him.”
translator_notes: From this narration on, the source usually begins directly with a shaykh of Ibn Abī ʿUmar (Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā, Sufyān, Wakīʿ, etc.), the frame being understood. ‘ʿAbd Allāh’ is presumably Ibn Masʿūd (Abū ʿUbayda being his son), but the source gives only ‘ʿAbd Allāh’.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ عِيسَى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ خَيْثَمَةَ، عَنْ عَدِيِّ بْنِ حَاتِمٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.matn_ar: «مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا سَيُكَلِّمُهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهُ تَرْجُمَانٌ»
records.isnad_en: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā narrated to us. He said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Khaythama, from ʿAdī b. Ḥātim, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “There is none of you but God will speak to him on the Day of Resurrection, with no interpreter between him and Him.”
translator_notes: A longer form of this report is no. 24.

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on the obligations of Islam and its shares

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ عِيسَى،
records.matn_ar: قَالَ الْأَعْمَشُ: حُدِّثْنَا عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ مُرَّةَ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ الْأَخْرَمِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَوْ عَنْ عَمِّهِ - شَكَّ الْأَعْمَشُ - قَالَ: أَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَهُ، فَاسْتَقْبَلْتُهُ، فَصَاحَ بِي نَاسٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ، فقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: «دَعُوهُ فَأَرَبٌ مَا جَاءَ بِهِ» فَأَخَذْتُ بِزِمَامِ النَّاقَةِ فقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، دُلَّنِي عَلَى عَمَلٍ يُقَرِّبُنِي مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ، وَيُبَاعِدُنِي مِنَ النَّارِ، قَالَ: «إِنْ كُنْتَ أَوْجَزْتَ» فَسَكَتَ سَاعَةً، ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فقَالَ: «تَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَتُقِيمُ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِي الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومُ رَمَضَانَ، وَتُحِبُّ لِلنَّاسِ مَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ يُؤْتَى إِلَيْكَ، وَمَا كَرِهْتَ أَنْ يُؤْتَى إِلَيْكَ فَدَعِ النَّاسَ مِنْهُ خَلِّ عَنْ زِمَامِ النَّاقَةِ»
records.isnad_en: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā narrated to us. He said: al-Aʿmash said: It was narrated to us from ʿAmr b. Murra, from al-Mughīra b. Saʿd al-Akhram, from his father or his uncle—al-Aʿmash was unsure—who said:
records.matn_en: I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ wishing to ask him, and I approached him, and some of his Companions shouted at me. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Leave him, for he has some need in coming.” So I took hold of the camel’s halter and said: O Messenger of God, direct me to a deed that will bring me near to Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: “If you have been brief…” and he was silent for a while, then raised his head to the sky and said: “You worship God and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give the zakāt, fast Ramaḍān, and love for people what you love to be done to you; and what you dislike to be done to you, leave people from it. Let go of the camel’s halter.”
translator_notes: al-Aʿmash received this through unnamed informants (‘it was narrated to us’). The phrase ‘If you have been brief’ is elliptical in the source; the rendering is tentative.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ سُعَيْرِ بْنِ الْخِمْسِ التَّمِيمِيِّ، عَنْ حَبِيبِ بْنِ أَبِي ثَابِتٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: " بُنِيَ الْإِسْلَامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَصَوْمِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Suʿayr b. al-Khimṣ al-Tamīmī, from Ḥabīb b. Abī Thābit, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Islam is built on five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakāt, the fast of the month of Ramaḍān, and the pilgrimage to the House.”
translator_notes: ‘Sufyān’ is presumably Sufyān b. ʿUyayna, who is named in full in no. 20.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ السَّرِيِّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: قَالَ عَلِيٌّ: " خُذُوا مِنِّي هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الْخَمْسَ، فَإِنَّكُمْ وَاللَّهِ لَوْ رَكِبْتُمُ الْمَطِيَّ حَتَّى تَنْصِبُوهَا مَا أَدْرَكْتُمْ مِثْلَهُنَّ: لَا يَرْجُو عَبْدٌ إِلَّا رَبَّهُ، وَلَا يَخَافَنَّ إِلَّا ذَنْبَهُ، وَلَا يَسْتَحِي إِذَا سُئِلَ عَمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُ أَنْ يَقُولَ: لَا أَعْلَمُ، وَلَا يَسْتَحِي أَنْ يَتَعَلَّمَ إِذَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ، وَأَنَّ الصَّبْرَ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ، بِمَنْزِلَةِ الرَّأْسِ مِنَ الْجَسَدِ، لَا خَيْرَ فِي جَسَدٍ لَا رَأْسَ لَهُ "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Sarī b. Ismāʿīl, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: ʿAlī said:
records.matn_en: “Take from me these five words, for by God, if you were to ride the mounts until you wore them out, you would not find their like: Let no servant hope for anything but his Lord, and let him fear nothing but his sin; let him not be ashamed, when asked about what he does not know, to say ‘I do not know’; and let him not be ashamed to learn when he does not know; and patience is to faith as the head is to the body—there is no good in a body that has no head.”

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَمْزَةَ الثُّمَالِيُّ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: دَخَلَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْأَهْتَمِ عَلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ، فقَالَ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَتُحِبُّ أَنْ أُطْرِيَكَ؟ قَالَ: «لَا» قَالَ: فَتُحِبُّ أَنْ أَعِظَكَ؟ فقَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَأثْنَى عَلَيْهِ، وقَالَ: " أَمَّا بَعْدُ: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ ⦗ص: 86⦘ وَجَلَّ بِجَلَالِهِ وَعَظَمَتِهِ، وقُدْرَتِهِ، خَلَقَ الْخَلْقَ، غَنِيًّا عَنْ طَاعَتِهِمْ، آمِنًا لِمَعْصِيَتِهِمْ، وَالنَّاسُ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُخْتَلِفُونَ فِي الرَّأْيِ وَالْمَنَازِلِ، وَالْعَرَبُ بِشَرِّ تِلْكَ الْمَنَازِلِ، أَهْلُ الدَّبَرِ، وَأَهْلُ الْوَبَرِ، وَأَهْلُ الْحَجَرِ، وَأَهْلُ الْحَضَرِ، تُحْتَازُ دُونَهُمْ طَيِّبَاتُ الدُّنْيَا ورَخَاءُ عَيْشِهَا، لَا يَسْأَلُونَ اللَّهَ جَمَاعَةً، وَلَا يَتْلُونَ كِتَابًا، حَيُّهُمْ أَعْمَى، نَجِسٌ، وَمَيِّتُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ، مَعَ مَا لَا يُحْصَى مِنَ الْمَزْهُودِ فِيهِ وَالْمَرْغُوبِ عَنْهُ، فَلَمَّا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَبْعَثَ إِلَيْهِمْ نَبِيَّهُمْ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَيَنْشُرَ فِيهِمْ رَحْمَتَهُ، بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ، عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ، حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ، بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ، مُحَمَّدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم. فَلَمْ يَمْنَعْهُمْ ذَلِكَ أَنْ جَرَحُوهُ فِي جِسْمِهِ، وَلَقَّبُوهُ فِي اسْمِهِ، وَأَخْرَجُوهُ مِنْ دَارِهِ، وَمَعَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ، لَا يُتَقَدَّمُ إِلَّا بِأَمْرِهِ، وَلَا يُرْحَلُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ، وَقَدْ أَخَذَ حَبْلَ الذِّمَّةِ مِنَ الْأَعْلَى، وَقَدِ اضْطَرُّوهُ إِلَى بَطْنِ غَارٍ، فَاخْتَفَى فِيهِ اخْتِفَاءً، فَلَمَّا أُمِرَ بِالْعَزْمِ، وَحُمِلَ عَلَى الْجِهَادِ، اسْبَطَرَ لِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ لَوْثُهُ، وَقَدِ اسْتَقَامَ عَلَى الَّذِي أَمَرَهُ اللَّهُ بِهِ مِنْ تَبْلِيغِ رِسَالَتِهِ، وَمُجَاهَدَةِ الْمُدْبِرِ، حَتَّى قَبَضَهُ اللَّهُ، وَقَدْ أَدَّى الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ مِنْ حَقِّهِ، ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ قَامَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ، فَأَخَذَ بِسُنَّتِهِ، وَدَعَا إِلَى سَبِيلِهِ، وَمَضَى عَلَى أمْرِهِ، حَيْثُ ارْتَدَّتِ الْعَرَبُ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ مَنِ ارْتَدَّ مِنْهُمْ، فَحَرَصُوا أَنْ يُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ، وَلَا يُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ، فَأَبَى أَنْ يَقْبَلَ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا مَا كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَابِلًا مِنْهُمْ فِي حَيَاتِهِ، فَانْتَزَعَ السُّيوفَ مِنْ أغْمَادِها ⦗ص: 87⦘ وَأَوْقَدَ النَّارَ فِي شُعُلِهَا، وَحَمَلَ أَهْلَ الْحَقِّ عَلَى أَكْتَافِ أَهْلِ الْبَاطِلِ، فَلَمْ يَبْرَحْ يُقَطِّعُ أَوْصَالَهُمْ، وَيَسْقِي الْأَرْضَ دِمَاءَهُمْ، حَتَّى أَدْخَلَهُمْ فِي الْبَابِ الَّذِي خَرَجُوا مِنْهُ، وقَرَّرْهُمْ بِالَّذِي نَفَرُوا عَنْهُ فَقَبَضَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ، عَلَى مِنْهَاجِ نَبِيِّهِ، ورَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ وَغَفَرَ لَهُ "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna narrated to us. He said: Abū Ḥamza al-Thumālī informed us. He said:
records.matn_en: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ahtam entered upon ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and said: O Commander of the Faithful, would you like me to praise you? He said: “No.” He said: Would you like me to admonish you? He said: Yes. So he praised God and extolled Him, and said: “To proceed: God, mighty and majestic, in His majesty, His greatness and His power, created creation, being free of need of their obedience and secure against their disobedience. People at that time differed in opinion and standing, and the Arabs were in the worst of those stations: the people of the saddle-sore (ahl al-dabar), the people of camel hair (ahl al-wabar), the people of stone (ahl al-ḥajar) and the people of settled habitation (ahl al-ḥaḍar); the good things of the world and the ease of its living were gathered up to the exclusion of them. They did not ask God in congregation and did not recite a book; their living were blind and impure, and their dead were in the Fire, together with what cannot be counted of things to be shunned and turned away from. Then, when God willed to send to them their Prophet ﷺ and to spread His mercy among them, He raised among them a messenger from among themselves, grievous to him is what you suffer, anxious over you, to the believers compassionate and merciful: Muḥammad ﷺ. Yet that did not stop them from wounding him in his body, giving him nicknames in place of his name, and driving him out of his home, while he had with him an admonition from his Lord: no step forward except by His command, and no departure except by His leave. He had taken the rope of protection (dhimma) from the Most High, and they had forced him into the belly of a cave, where he hid himself. Then, when he was commanded to resolve and was charged with jihad, his hesitation gave way (isbaṭarra lawthuhu) to God’s command, and he kept steadfastly to what God commanded him—conveying His message and striving against the one who turns away—until God took him, having discharged what he owed of His right. Then Abū Bakr rose after him, took up his sunna, called to his path and proceeded on his course, when the Arabs apostatized against him, or those of them who apostatized, and they were keen to establish the prayer but not to give the zakāt. He refused to accept from them anything except what the Messenger of God ﷺ had accepted from them in his lifetime. So he drew the swords from their scabbards [p. 87], kindled the fire in its flames, and set the people of truth upon the shoulders of the people of falsehood; he did not cease cutting their limbs and watering the earth with their blood, until he brought them back into the door from which they had gone out and made them acknowledge what they had shunned. Then God took him to Himself, on the way of his Prophet; may God have mercy on him and forgive him.”
translator_notes: This is an address delivered to ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, not a ḥadīth of the Prophet. Several rare expressions (ahl al-dabar, isbaṭarra lawthuhu, and the phrase on the ‘rope of protection’) are obscure; the rendering is tentative in these places. The source has an opening quotation mark before ‘To proceed’ and a closing one at the end.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: قِيلَ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ: اقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ لَا يُؤَدُّوا الزَّكَاةَ، فقَالَ: لَوْ مَنَعُونِي شَيْئًا مِمَّا أَقَرُّوا بِهِ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ، لَقَاتَلْتُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ، فَقِيلَ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ: أَلَيْسَ قَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم " أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، فَإِذَا قَالُوهَا عَصَمُوا مِنِّي دِمَاءَهُمْ وأمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَّا بِحَقِّهَا وَحِسَابُهُمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ؟ " فقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: هَذَا مِنْ حَقِّهَا، لَوْ مَنَعُونِي شَيْئًا مِمَّا أَعْطَوْا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، لَقَاتَلْتُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ، لَا تُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ مَا جَمَعَ اللَّهُ قَالَ سُفْيَانُ: «يَعْنِي الصَّلَاةَ وَالزَّكَاةَ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said:
records.matn_en: Abū Bakr was told: Accept from them that they not pay the zakāt. He said: If they withheld from me anything of what they had affirmed to the Messenger of God, I would fight them over it. It was said to Abū Bakr: Did the Messenger of God ﷺ not say: “I have been commanded to fight people until they say: There is no god but God; and when they say it, they protect from me their blood and their wealth, except by its right, and their reckoning is with God”? Abū Bakr said: This is part of its right. If they withheld from me anything of what they gave to the Messenger of God, I would fight them over it. Do not separate between what God has joined. Sufyān said: “Meaning the prayer and the zakāt.”
translator_notes: Mursal: al-Zuhrī relates an event after the Prophet’s death without naming his source. The comment at the end is by Sufyān.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Maintaining ablution is part of faith
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ الْمُحافَظَةُ عَلَى الْوُضُوءِ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ سَالِمِ بْنِ أَبِي الْجَعْدِ، عَنْ ثَوْبَانَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: «اسْتَقِيمُوا وَلَنْ تُحْصُوا، واعْلَمُوا أَنَّ خَيْرَ أَعْمَالِكُمُ الصَّلَاةُ وَلَا يُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْوُضُوءِ إِلَّا مُؤْمِنٌ» . حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ سَالِمِ بْنِ أَبِي الْجَعْدِ، عَنْ ثَوْبَانَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَحْوَهُ
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim b. Abī al-Jaʿd, from Thawbān, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Be upright, though you will never fully encompass it; and know that the best of your works is the prayer, and none maintains ablution except a believer.” Wakīʿ narrated to us. He said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Sālim b. Abī al-Jaʿd, from Thawbān, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
translator_notes: The numbering passes from 21 to 23; no. 22 is not present in this export. The record continues with a second chain (Wakīʿ ← al-Aʿmash ← Sālim ← Thawbān), given here after the text as printed.

groups.title_en: Chapter on the speech of God, mighty and majestic, and the seeing of Him on the Day of Resurrection
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ فِي كَلَامِ اللَّهِ عز وجل وَرُؤْيَتِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ عِيسَى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ خَيْثَمَةَ، عَنْ عَدِيِّ بْنِ حَاتِمٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.matn_ar: «مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ، إِلَّا سَيُكَلِّمُهُ اللَّهُ، لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهُ تَرْجُمانٌ فَيَنْظُرُ ⦗ص: 90⦘ أيْمَنَ مِنْهُ فَلَا يَرَى إِلَّا مَا قَدَّمَ، وَيَنْظُرُ أشْأَمَ مِنْهُ فَلَا يَرَى إِلَّا مَا قَدَّمَ، وَيَنْظُرُ أمَامَهُ فَيَرَى النَّارَ، فَمَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَقِيَ وَجْهَهُ عَنِ النَّارِ وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ فَلْيَفْعَلْ»
records.isnad_en: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā narrated to us. He said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Khaythama, from ʿAdī b. Ḥātim, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “There is none of you but God will speak to him, with no interpreter between him and Him. He will look [p. 90] to his right and see only what he has sent ahead; he will look to his left and see only what he has sent ahead; and he will look before him and see the Fire. So whoever of you is able to shield his face from the Fire, even with half a date, let him do so.”
translator_notes: This is a longer form of no. 16. The page marker [p. 90] falls in the middle of the sentence in the source.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Congregational prayer is among the ways of guidance (sunan al-hudā)
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ صَلَاةُ الْجَمَاعَةِ مِنْ سُنَنِ الْهُدَى

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الْهَجَرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي الْأَحْوَصِ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: «مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَلْقَى اللَّهَ غَدًا مُسْلِمًا فَلْيُحَافِظْ عَلَى هَذِهِ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْمَكْتُوبَاتِ حَيْثُ يُنَادِي بِهِنَّ، فَإِنَّهُنَّ مِنْ سُنَنِ الْهُدَى، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَرَعَ لِنَبِيِّكُمْ صلى الله عليه وسلم سُنُنَ الْهُدَى ولَقَدْ رَأَيْتَنَا وَمَا يَتَخَلَّفُ عَنْهَا إِلَّا مُنَافِقٌ مَعْلُومٌ نِفاقُهُ حَتَّى لَقَدْ رأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ يُهَادَى بَيْنَ الرَّجُلَيْنِ حَتَّى يُقَامَ فِي الصَّفِّ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Hajarī, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd say:
records.matn_en: “Whoever would be pleased to meet God tomorrow as a Muslim, let him maintain these prescribed prayers wherever they are called, for they are among the ways of guidance (sunan al-hudā), and God has laid down for your Prophet ﷺ the ways of guidance. And we have seen ourselves [at a time when] none stayed away from it except a hypocrite whose hypocrisy was known, such that I saw a man being supported between two men until he was stood in the row.”

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on the application of the term ‘disbelief’ to one who abandons prayer
groups.title_ar: تَابِعُ بَابِ إِطْلَاقِ الْكُفْرِ عَلَى مَنْ تَرَكَ الصَّلَاةَ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا الْمُقْرِئُ،
records.matn_ar: 26 - عَنِ الْمَسْعُودِيِّ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: قِيلَ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَيُكْثِرُ ذِكْرَ الصَّلَاةِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ {الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِمْ دَائِمُونَ} [المعارج: 23] الْمَعَارِجُ وَ {الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ} [المؤمنون: 2] الْمُؤْمِنُونَ، فقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: «عَلَى مَواقِيتِها» ، فَقِيلَ: مَا كُنَّا نَرَى ذَاكَ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، إِلَّا أَنْ تُتْرَكَ؟، فقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: «تَرْكُهَا كُفْرٌ»
records.isnad_en: al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, from al-Masʿūdī, from al-Ḥasan b. Saʿd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd, who said:
records.matn_en: ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd was told: God mentions prayer abundantly in the Qurʾān: “Those who are constant in their prayer” [Q. 70:23] (al-Maʿārij) and “Those who in their prayers are humble” [Q. 23:2] (al-Muʾminūn). ʿAbd Allāh said: “[It means] at its appointed times.” It was said: We only understood that to mean that it not be abandoned, O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān? ʿAbd Allāh said: “Abandoning it is disbelief.”

narrators.en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd

translator_notes: The number 26 is printed in the middle of the isnad, between ‘al-Muqriʾ narrated to us’ and ‘from al-Masʿūdī’. The question put to ʿAbd Allāh is by unnamed persons, and the rendering of their reply is tentative.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The inviolability of the blood and property of the believer

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا الْمُقْرِئُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَنِ الْمُسْلِمُ؟، قَالَ: «مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ» قَالَ: فَمَنِ الْمُؤْمِنُ؟ قَالَ: «مَنْ أَمِنَهُ النَّاسُ عَلَى أَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ» قَالَ: فَمَنِ الْمُهَاجِرُ؟ قَالَ: «مَنْ هَجَرَ السَّيِّئاتِ» قَالَ: فَمَنِ الْمُجَاهِدُ؟ قَالَ: «مَنْ جَاهَدَ نَفْسَهُ للَّهِ تَعَالَى»
records.isnad_en: al-Muqriʾ narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Ziyād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr, who said:
records.matn_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of God, who is the Muslim? He said: “The one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.” He said: Who is the believer? He said: “The one whom people trust with their wealth and their lives.” He said: Who is the emigrant (muhājir)? He said: “The one who abandons evil deeds.” He said: Who is the one who strives (mujāhid)? He said: “The one who strives against his own self for God Almighty.”

groups.title_en: Chapter on the increase and decrease of faith

records.isnad_ar: قَالَ سُفْيَانُ:
records.matn_ar: «الْإِيمَانُ قَوْلٌ وَعَمَلٌ يَزِيدُ وَيَنْقُصُ» وقَالَ لَهُ أَخوهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ: يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ، لَا تَقُلْ يَنْقُصُ، فَغَضِبَ وقَالَ: «اسْكُتْ يَا صَبِيُّ، بَلْ يَنْقُصُ حَتَّى لَا يَبْقَى مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān said:
records.matn_en: “Faith is word and deed; it increases and decreases.” His brother Ibrāhīm b. ʿUyayna said to him: O Abū Muḥammad, do not say ‘it decreases’. He grew angry and said: “Be quiet, boy! Rather, it decreases until nothing of it remains.”
translator_notes: The heading and the number 28 are printed together in the source. ‘Sufyān’ is Sufyān b. ʿUyayna (Abū Muḥammad), as the mention of his brother Ibrāhīm shows. This is a saying of Sufyān, not a report with a chain.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The statements of the Murjiʾa and the Jahmiyya on faith
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ أَقْوَالُ الْمُرْجِئَةِ وَالْجَهْمِيَّةِ فِي الْإِيمَانِ

records.isnad_ar: قَالَ 29 - أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ
records.matn_ar: قَالَ وَكِيعٌ: " أَهْلُ السُّنَّةِ يَقُولُونَ: الْإِيمَانُ قَوْلٌ وَعَمَلٌ، وَالْمُرْجِئَةُ يَقُولُونَ: إِنَّ الْإِيمَانَ قَوْلٌ بِلَا عَمَلٍ، وَالْجَهْمِيَّةُ يَقُولُونَ: إِنَّ الْإِيمَانَ الْمَعْرِفَةُ "
records.isnad_en: He said: Abū Aḥmad informed us. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us. He said: Wakīʿ [said]:
records.matn_en: “The people of the Sunna say: Faith is word and deed; the Murjiʾa say: Faith is word without deed; and the Jahmiyya say: Faith is knowledge (al-maʿrifa).”
translator_notes: The number 29 is printed after an opening ‘He said’ at the start of the line. The frame is abbreviated and Wakīʿ’s statement is introduced only by ‘Wakīʿ said’; it is a saying of Wakīʿ, not a report with a full chain.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The obligation of calm (ṭumaʾnīna) in prayer, and that it is part of faith
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ وُجُوبُ الطُّمَأْنِينَةِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَأَنَّهَا مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَبْصَرَ رَجُلًا يُصَلِّي يَنْقُرُ كَمَا يَنْقُرُ الْغُرَابُ، فقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لَوْ مَاتَ هَذَا، مَاتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ دِينِ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم» . حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ صَبِيحٍ الْخُرَاسَانِيِّ، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَابِطٍ الْجُمَحِيِّ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِثْلَهُ
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ
records.matn_en: saw a man praying, pecking as a crow pecks, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “If this man were to die, he would die on other than the religion of Muḥammad ﷺ.” Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā b. Ṣubayḥ al-Khurāsānī, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from ʿAmr b. Dīnār, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sābiṭ al-Jumaḥī, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
translator_notes: Mursal: Jaʿfar’s father does not name a Companion, and the second chain (through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sābiṭ) likewise goes directly to the Prophet. The second chain is given after the text, as in the source.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The concern of the early generations (salaf) for performing prayer
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ حِرْصُ السَّلَفِ عَلَى أَدَاءِ الصَّلَاةِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ السَّخْتِيَانِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ، عَنِ الْمِسْوَرِ بْنِ مَخْرَمَةَ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: لَمَّا طُعِنَ عُمَرُ، قَالَ ⦗ص: 99⦘ : «إِنَّكُمْ لَسْتُمْ تَفْزَعُونَ لِشَيْءٍ إِنْ كَانَتْ بِهِ حَيَاةٌ إِلَّا بِالصَّلَاةِ» ، فقَالُوا: الصَّلَاةُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ؟ قَالَ: «الصَّلَاةُ، وَلَا حَظَّ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ لِمَنْ تَرَكَ الصَّلَاةَ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, from Ibn Abī Mulayka, from al-Miswar b. Makhrama, who said:
records.matn_en: When ʿUmar was stabbed, he said [p. 99]: “You would not rouse anything in which there is life by anything but the prayer.” They said: The prayer, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: “The prayer! And there is no share in Islam for one who abandons the prayer.”
translator_notes: The first sentence of ʿUmar’s statement is terse; the sense appears to be that only the call ‘the prayer!’ would rouse him if he were still alive. The rendering is tentative.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَجْلَانَ وَيَزِيدَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ سَمِعَا مَكْحُولًا يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: أَوْصَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَعْضَ أَهْلِهِ، فقَالَ: «وَلَا تَتْرُكَنَّ صَلَاةً مُتَعَمِّدًا، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ تَرَكَ صَلَاةً مَكْتُوبَةً مُتَعَمِّدًا فَقَدْ بَرِئَتْ مِنْهُ ذِمَّةُ اللَّهِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān and Yazīd b. Yazīd b. Jābir—both of them heard Makḥūl say:
records.matn_en: The Prophet ﷺ gave counsel to one of his household and said: “Do not ever abandon a prayer deliberately, for whoever abandons a prescribed prayer deliberately, the protection (dhimma) of God is clear of him.”
translator_notes: Mursal: Makḥūl does not name a Companion, and the source does not name the member of the household.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Fighting over abandoning the pilgrimage

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي هِنْدٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: أَرَادَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ أَنْ يَعْرِضَ عَلَى النَّاسِ عِدَّةً فِي كُلِّ بَلَدٍ يُوَافُونَ الْحَجَّ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ، فَلَمَّا رَأَى تَسَارُعَ النَّاسِ فِيهِ، كَفَّ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وقَالَ: «لَوْ تَرَكُوهُ، لَجَاهَدْنَاهُمْ عَلَيْهِ كَمَا نُجَاهِدُهُمْ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Dāwūd b. Abī Hind, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, who said:
records.matn_en: ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb wanted to assign to the people a set number from every land who would attend the pilgrimage each year; but when he saw how quickly people hastened to it, he refrained from that and said: “Had they abandoned it, we would have fought them over it just as we fight them over the prayer and the zakāt.”
translator_notes: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reports an event of ʿUmar’s time without naming his source. The opening phrase (‘yaʿriḍa ʿalā al-nās ʿidda’) is terse; the rendering is tentative.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The decrease of faith through the decrease of acts of obedience

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ ذَرٍّ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ، عَنْ وَائِلِ بْنِ مَهَانَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: «يَا مَعْشَرَ النِّسَاءِ، تَصَدَّقْنَ وَلَوْ مِنْ حُلِيِّكُنَّ، فَإِنَّكُنْ مِنْ أَكْثَرِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ» فَقَامَتِ امْرَأَةٌ لَيْسَتْ مِنْ عِلْيَةِ النِّسَاءِ، فقَالَتْ: وَلِمَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: «إِنَّكُنَّ تُكْثِرْنَ اللَّعْنَ، وتَجْحُدْنَ النِّعَمَ، وَتَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ» قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: مَا وَجَدْنَا مِنْ نَاقِصِ الْعَقْلِ وَالدِّينِ أَغْلَبَ عَلَى عُقُولِ الرِّجَالِ ذَوِي الرَّأْيِ عَلَى أُمُورِهِمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ: يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، مَا نُقْصَانُ عَقْلِها ودِينِهَا؟ فقَالَ: أَمَّا نُقْصَانُ عَقْلِها فَشَهَادَةُ امْرَأَتَيْنِ بِشَهادَةِ رَجُلٍ، وَأَمَّا نُقْصَانُ دِينِهَا فَإِنَّهَا تَمْكُثُ كَذَا وكَذَا لَا تُصَلِّي لِلَّهِ سَجْدَةً
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Dharr al-Hamdānī, from Wāʾil b. Mahāna, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “O company of women, give charity, even from your jewelry, for you are the majority of the people of the Fire.” A woman who was not among the elite of the women stood up and said: Why, O Messenger of God? He said: “You curse much, deny favors, and are ungrateful to the spouse (al-ʿashīr).” ʿAbd Allāh said: We have not found any more deficient in intellect and religion, yet more overpowering of the minds of men of sound judgment in their affairs, than women. He was asked: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what is the deficiency of her intellect and religion? He said: As for the deficiency of her intellect, it is that the testimony of two women is equal to the testimony of one man; and as for the deficiency of her religion, it is that she remains so many days not praying a single prostration to God.
translator_notes: The explanation of ‘deficiency in intellect and religion’ is given in the source as the words of ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd), after the Prophet’s words. The woman who speaks is not named; ‘not among the elite of the women’ is the source’s description of her.

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on faith in divine decree (al-qadar)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُدْعَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي نَضْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: " أَلَا وَإِنَّ بَنِي آدَمَ خُلِقُوا عَلَى طَبَقَاتٍ: فمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُولَدُ مُؤْمِنًا وَيَحْيَا مُؤْمِنًا ويَمُوتُ مُؤْمِنًا، ومِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُولَدُ كَافِرًا وَيَحْيَا كَافِرًا ويَمُوتُ كَافِرًا، ومِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُولَدُ مُؤْمِنًا وَيَحْيَا مُؤْمِنًا وَيَمُوتُ كَافِرًا، ومِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُولَدُ كَافِرًا وَيَحْيَا كَافِرًا ويَمُوتُ مُؤْمِنًا "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Judʿān, from Abū Naḍra, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (r), who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Indeed, the children of Adam were created in tiers: among them is he who is born a believer, lives a believer and dies a believer; among them is he who is born a disbeliever, lives a disbeliever and dies a disbeliever; among them is he who is born a believer, lives a believer and dies a disbeliever; and among them is he who is born a disbeliever, lives a disbeliever and dies a believer.”

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on fighting over abandoning the pilgrimage
groups.title_ar: تَابِعُ بَابِ الْمُجَاهَدَةِ عَلَى تَرْكِ الْحَجِّ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: وَحُدِّثْتُ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَابِطٍ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ زَادٌ وَرَاحِلَةٌ، فَلَمْ يَحُجَّ، وَلَمْ يَحْبِسْهُ مَرَضٌ حَابِسٌ، أَوْ سُلْطَانٌ جَائرٌ، أَوْ حاجَةٌ ظَاهِرَةٌ، فَلْيَمُتْ يَهُودِيًّا، أَوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا، أَوْ مَيْتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً»
records.isnad_en: Hishām narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: And it was narrated to me from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Sābiṭ, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Whoever has provisions and a mount and does not perform the pilgrimage, and is not held back by a detaining illness, or an unjust ruler, or an evident need, let him die a Jew or a Christian, or a death of the Jāhiliyya.”

narrators.en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Sābiṭ

translator_notes: Mursal, with an unnamed informant between Ibn Jurayj and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Sābiṭ (‘ḥuddithtu’, ‘it was narrated to me’); no Companion is named. ‘Hishām’ is not further identified in the source.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ نُعَيْمٍ،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ الضَّحَّاكَ بْنَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَرْزَمٍ الْأَشْعَرِيَّ، أخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، قَالَ: «لِيَمُتْ يَهُودِيًّا أوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا - ثَلَاثَ مرَّاتٍ ⦗ص: 106⦘ ، رَجُلٌ مَاتَ وَلَمْ يَحُجَّ، وَجَدَ لِذَلِكَ سَعَةً، وخُلِّيَتْ سَبِيلُهُ»
records.isnad_en: Hishām narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAbd Allāh b. Nuʿaym informed me, that al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿArzam al-Ashʿarī informed him, that ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb said:
records.matn_en: “Let him die a Jew or a Christian”—three times [p. 106]—“a man who died without having performed the pilgrimage, having found ample means for it and his way being clear.”

narrators.en: al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿArzam al-Ashʿarī

translator_notes: The page marker [p. 106] appears inside a record labelled p. 105. The wording ‘that ʿUmar said’ is as printed; no intermediary is named between al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿUmar.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ دِينَارٍ،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ حَسَنَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ، أخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، «رَأَى نَاسًا بِعَرَفَةَ، فِي الْحَجِّ عَلَيْهِمْ قُمُصٌ وَعَمَائِمُ، فَضَرَبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْجِزْيَةَ» . فقُلْتُ: مِمَّنْ هُمْ؟ قَالَ: لَا أدْرِي، قُلْتُ: أيْنَ رَآهُمْ؟ قَالَ: لَا أدْرِي
records.isnad_en: Hishām narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAmr b. Dīnār informed me, that Ḥasan b. Muḥammad informed him, that ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb
records.matn_en: saw people at ʿArafa during the pilgrimage wearing shirts and turbans, and he imposed the jizya on them. I said: Who were they? He said: I do not know. I said: Where did he see them? He said: I do not know.
translator_notes: Ḥasan b. Muḥammad reports ‘that ʿUmar’ without naming an intermediary. The final two questions and answers are presumably between Ibn Jurayj and ʿAmr b. Dīnār; the source does not mark the speakers.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، قَالَ ⦗ص: 107⦘ : أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ مَوْلًى لَنَا، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ بْنِ أَبِي السَّائِبِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَهُ يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: سَمِعْتُ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، يَقُولُ: «مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ حَجَّ فَلْيَحُجَّ الْعَامَ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَعَامٌ قَابِلٌ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَعَامٌ قَابِلٌ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أوْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ، كَتَبْنَا فِي يَدِهِ يَهُودِيًّا أوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا»
records.isnad_en: Hishām narrated to us. He said [p. 107]: Ibn Jurayj informed me. He said: Sulaymān, a freedman of ours, informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Musayyab b. Abī al-Sāʾib, that he heard him say: I heard ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb say:
records.matn_en: “Whoever has not performed the pilgrimage, let him perform it this year; if he is unable, then next year; if he is unable, then next year; and if he is unable or does not do so, we will write on his hand: a Jew or a Christian.”

narrators.en: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Musayyab b. Abī al-Sāʾib

translator_notes: The source’s ‘that he heard him say: I heard ʿUmar’ moves between two speakers (ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Musayyab and the person he reports); it is rendered as printed.

groups.title_en: Chapter on the lifting of trust and faith from some hearts
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ فِي رَفْعِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَالْإِيمَانِ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْقُلُوبِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ حُذَيْفَةَ، يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: «وَيَظَلُّ النَّاسُ يَتَبَايَعُونَ وَلَيْسَ فِيهِمْ رَجُلٌ يُؤَدِّي الْأَمَانَةَ، حَتَّى يُقَالَ لِلرَّجُلِ مَا أجْلَدَهُ، وَمَا أظْرَفَهُ، وَمَا أعْقَلَهُ، وَمَا فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ مِنْ إِيمَانٍ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Zayd b. Wahb, who said: I heard Ḥudhayfa say:
records.matn_en: “People will go on trading with one another, and there will not be among them a man who fulfils his trust, until it is said of a man: How sturdy he is! How refined he is! How intelligent he is!—while there is not in his heart a mustard-seed’s weight of faith.”

groups.title_en: Chapter: The departure of faith upon committing acts of disobedience
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ فِي زَوَالِ الْإِيمَانِ عِنْدَ ارْتِكَابِ الْمَعَاصِي

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ الْمُلَيْكِيِّ، عَنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْلَةَ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «مَا الْإِيمَانُ إِلَّا بِمَنْزِلَةِ قَمِيصِ أَحَدِكُمْ، يَلْبَسُهُ مَرَّةً، وَيَنْزِعُهُ مَرَّةً»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-Mulaykī, from Ibrāhīm b. Abī ʿAbla, from a man, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, that he said:
records.matn_en: “Faith is nothing but like the shirt of one of you: he wears it at one time and takes it off at another.”
translator_notes: The chain contains an unnamed man (‘from a man’) between Ibrāhīm b. Abī ʿAbla and Abū al-Dardāʾ.

records.isnad_ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ:
records.matn_ar: «مَا أَمِنَ عَبْدٌ قَطُّ أَنْ يُسْلَبَ إِيمَانُهُ إِلَّا سُلِبَهُ سَرِيعًا، ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُ لَهُ فَقْدًا»
records.isnad_en: Then Abū al-Dardāʾ said:
records.matn_en: “No servant has ever felt secure that his faith would not be stripped from him but it was stripped from him swiftly, and then he does not even feel its loss.”
translator_notes: No number is printed in the source; this continues no. 42 as a further saying of Abū al-Dardāʾ.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Righteous work raises the good word
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ الْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُ الْكَلَامَ الطَّيِّبَ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا لَيْثُ بْنُ أَبِي سُلَيْمٍ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى
records.matn_ar: {إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ} [فاطر: 10] فَاطِرٌ قَالَ: «الْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُ الْكَلَامَ الطَّيِّبَ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us. He said: Layth b. Abī Sulaym narrated to us, from Shahr b. Ḥawshab, regarding the saying of God Almighty:
records.matn_en: “To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it” [Q. 35:10] (Fāṭir). He said: “The righteous deed raises the good word.”
translator_notes: Shahr’s comment takes the righteous deed as the subject of ‘raises it’. The sūra name Fāṭir is added after the verse in the source.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Modesty (ḥayāʾ) is part of faith

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ:
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَرَّ بِرَجُلٍ يَعِظُ أخَاهُ فِي الْحَيَاءِ، فقَالَ: «الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father:
records.matn_en: That the Messenger of God ﷺ passed by a man who was admonishing his brother about modesty, and he said: “Modesty is part of faith.”
translator_notes: The source says only ‘Sālim, from his father’; the father is not named in the text.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Restraining the tongue in times of tribulation (fitna)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا زِيَادُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حُسَيْنٍ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us. He said: Ziyād b. Saʿd narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAlī b. Ḥusayn, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Part of the excellence of a person’s Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.”
translator_notes: Mursal: ʿAlī b. Ḥusayn does not name a Companion.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Simplicity of dress (al-badhādha) is part of faith

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ،
records.matn_ar: أوْ عَنْ عَمِّهِ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «تَعَلَّمُوا يَا هَؤُلَاءِ أَنَّ الْبَذَاذَةَ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān informed us, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, from Muḥammad b. Kaʿb b. Mālik, from his father or his uncle:
records.matn_en: That the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Know, you people, that simplicity of dress (al-badhādha) is part of faith.”
translator_notes: The narrator is unsure whether it was his father or his uncle.

groups.title_en: Chapter: False praise is incompatible with faith

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ الطَّائِيِّ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ طَارِقِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: «إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَا يَمْلِكُ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا، فَيُحْلَفُ لَهُ، إِنَّكَ لَذَيْتَ وَذَيْتَ فَلَعَلَّهُ لَا يَحْلَا مِنْهُ بِشَيْءٍ، ثُمَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ مِنْ دِينِهِ شَيْءٌ، قَدْ ذَهَبَ دِينُهُ» ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ {أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَنْ يَشَاءُ} [النساء: 49] إِلَى قَوْلِهِ {إِثْمًا مُبِينًا} [النساء: 50] "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb al-Ṭāʾī, from Qays b. Muslim, from Ṭāriq b. Shihāb, who said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say:
records.matn_en: “A man possesses neither harm nor benefit, and it is sworn to him: You are such and such; and perhaps he will gain nothing from him. Then he returns to his house with nothing of his religion remaining with him—his religion has gone.” Then ʿAbd Allāh recited: “Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, God purifies whom He wills” [Q. 4:49], up to His saying “a manifest sin” [Q. 4:50].
translator_notes: The passage is elliptical and the verb ‘lā yaḥlā’ appears to be garbled in the source; the rendering is tentative. The source ends with a closing quotation mark after the Qurʾānic citation, without a matching opening mark.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The command to obey the one in authority (walī al-amr) and to be sincere in works for God
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ فِي الْأَمْرِ بِطَاعَةِ وَلِيِّ الْأَمْرِ وَإِخْلَاصِ الْعَمَلِ للَّهِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: كَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، وعُمَرُ، يُعَلِّمَانِ الرَّجُلَ إِذَا دَخَلَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ يَقُولَانِ: «تَعَبُدَ اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَتُصَلِّيَ الصَّلَاةَ الَّتِي افْتَرَضَهَا اللَّهُ عز وجل عَليْكَ لِمِيقَاتِهَا، فَإِنَّ فِي تَفْرِيطِهَا الْهَلَكَةَ، وَتُؤَدِّيَ الزَّكَاةَ طَيِّبَةً بِهَا نَفْسُكَ، وتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وتَسْمَعَ وَتُطِيعَ لِمَنْ وَلَّاهُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْرَ» قَالَ: وَقَدْ قَالَا لِرَجُلٍ: «وَتَعْمَلَ لِلَّهِ وَلَا تَعْمَلَ لِلنَّاسِ»
records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, from Hishām, from Muḥammad b. Sīrīn, who said:
records.matn_en: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar used to teach a man, when he entered Islam, saying: “You worship God and associate nothing with Him; you pray the prayer that God, mighty and majestic, has made obligatory upon you at its appointed time, for in neglecting it lies destruction; you give the zakāt with a willing heart; you fast Ramaḍān; and you listen and obey whomever God has put in charge of the matter.” He said: And they said to a man: “And you work for God and do not work for people.”

groups.title_en: Chapter on partisanship (al-ʿaṣabiyya)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ السِّخْتِيَانِيِّ، عَنْ غَيْلَانَ بْنِ جَرِيرٍ، عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ رَبَاحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «مَنْ خَرَجَ مِنَ الطَّاعَةِ، وَفَارَقَ الْجَمَاعَةَ، فَمَاتَ، مَاتَ مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً، وَمَنْ قَاتَلَ تَحْتَ رَايَةِ عَصَبِيَّةٍ يَتَعَصَّبُ لِلْعَصَبِيَّةِ، وَيُقَاتِلُ ⦗ص: 116⦘ لِلْعَصَبَةِ، وَيَدْعُو إِلَى الْعَصَبَةِ، فَقِتْلَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb al-Sikhtiyānī, from Ghaylān b. Jarīr, from Ziyād b. Rabāḥ, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Whoever goes out from obedience and separates from the community and dies, dies a death of the Jāhiliyya; and whoever fights under the banner of partisanship, showing partisanship for partisanship, fighting [p. 116] for the clan (ʿaṣaba) and calling to the clan—his is a killing of the Jāhiliyya.”

groups.title_en: Chapter on following the Sunna

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: «مَنِ اسْتَنَّ بِسُنَّتِي فَهُوَ مِنِّي، وَمَنْ رَغِبَ عَنْ سُنَّتِي فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي، وَعَمَلٌ قَلِيلٌ فِي السُّنَّةِ، خَيْرٌ مِنْ كَثِيرٍ فِي بِدْعَةٍ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Whoever follows my sunna is of me; whoever turns away from my sunna is not of me; and a little work in accord with the sunna is better than much in innovation (bidʿa).”
translator_notes: Mursal: al-Ḥasan does not name a Companion.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The pillars of faith (daʿāʾim al-īmān)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ، وحَدَّثَنَا أصْحابُنا، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: قَالَ عَلِيٌّ: " الْإِيمَانُ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ دَعَائِمَ: عَلَى الصَّبْرِ، وَالْيَقِينِ، وَالْعَدْلِ، وَالْجِهَادِ. وَالصَّبْرُ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ شُعَبٍ: عَلَى الشَّوْقِ، وَالشَّفَقِ، وَالزَّهَادَةِ، وَالتَّرَقُّبِ لِلْمَوتِ. فَمَنِ اشْتَاقَ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ مَسَلَ عَنِ الشَّهَوَاتِ، وَمَنْ أشْفَقَ مِنَ النَّارِ رَجَعَ عَنِ الْحُرُماتِ، وَمَنْ زَهِدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا تَهَاوَنَ فِي الْمُصِيبَاتِ، وَمَنْ تَرَقَّبَ الْمَوْتَ سَارَعَ فِي الْخَيْراتِ. وَالْيَقِينُ عَلَى أَرْبَعُ شُعَبٍ: تَبْصِرَةِ الْفِطْنَةِ، وتَأْوِيلِ الْحِكْمَةِ، وَمَوْعِظَةِ الْعِبْرَةِ، وسُنَّةِ ⦗ص: 119⦘ الْأَوَّلِينَ، فَمَنْ تَبَصَّرَ الْفِطْنَةَ تَأَوَّلَ الْحِكْمَةَ، وَمَنْ تَأَوَّلَ الْحِكْمَةَ عَرَفَ الْعِبْرَةَ، وَمَنْ عَرَفَ الْعِبْرَةَ فَكَأَنَّمَا كَانَ فِي الْأَوَّلِينَ. وَالْعَدْلُ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ شُعَبٍ: عَلَى غَايِصِ الْفَهْمِ، وزَهْرَةِ الْعِلْمِ، وَشَرَائِعَ، وَرَوْضَةِ الْحِلْمِ، فَمَنْ فَهِمَ فَسَّرَ جَمِيلَ الْعِلْمِ، وَمَنْ عَرَفَ شَرَائِعَ الْحُكْمِ، وَمَنْ حَلُمَ لَمْ يُفَرِّطْ وعَاشَ فِي النَّاسِ مَحْمُودًا. وَالْجِهَادُ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ شُعَبٍ: عَلَى الْأَمْرِ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ، وَالنَّهْيِ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ، وَشَنَآنِ الْفَاسِقِينَ، وَالصِّدْقِ فِي الْمَوَاطِنِ، فَمَنَ أمَرَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ، شَدَّ ظَهْرَ الْمُؤْمِنَ، وَمَنْ نَهَى عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ، أَرْغَمَ أَنْفَ الْمُنَافِقِ، وَمَنْ صَدَقَ فِي الْمَوَاطِنِ، قَضَى الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ، وَمَنْ غَضِبَ لِلَّهِ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عز وجل لَهُ "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us. He said: I heard it from more than one person, and our companions narrated to us. He said: ʿAlī said:
records.matn_en: “Faith rests on four pillars: on patience, certainty, justice and jihad. Patience has four branches: longing, fear, renunciation and watchful expectation of death. Whoever longs for Paradise turns away from desires; whoever fears the Fire turns back from the forbidden things; whoever renounces the world makes light of afflictions; and whoever watches for death hastens to good deeds. Certainty has four branches: the insight of discernment, the interpretation of wisdom, the admonition of the lesson, and the way (sunna) [p. 119] of the ancients. Whoever has insight into discernment interprets wisdom; whoever interprets wisdom comes to know the lesson; and whoever comes to know the lesson is as though he had lived among the ancients. Justice has four branches: the depth of understanding, the flower of knowledge, the laws (sharāʾiʿ), and the garden of forbearance. Whoever understands explains the beauty of knowledge; whoever knows the laws of judgment…; and whoever is forbearing does not neglect and lives among people praised. Jihad has four branches: commanding the right, forbidding the wrong, hatred of the sinners, and truthfulness in the decisive positions (al-mawāṭin). Whoever commands the right strengthens the back of the believer; whoever forbids the wrong humbles the nose of the hypocrite; whoever is truthful in the decisive positions has discharged what he owed; and whoever is angry for God’s sake, God, mighty and majestic, is angry for him.”

narrators.en: (more than one person; our companions, unnamed)

translator_notes: The chain contains unnamed informants (‘more than one person’, ‘our companions’). This is a saying attributed to ʿAlī, not a report from the Prophet. Several expressions are rare or elliptical and the rendering is tentative; in particular, the clause ‘whoever knows the laws of judgment’ has no stated consequence in the source, and ‘al-mawāṭin’ (lit. ‘the stations/positions’) may refer to battle positions.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: وبَلَغَنِي عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ، قَالَ: " مَا عُبِدَ اللَّهُ بِمِثْلِ الْعَقْلِ، وَلَنْ يَبْلُغَ الْعَبْدُ حَقِيقَةَ الْإِيمَانِ حَتَّى يَكُونَ فِيهِ عَشْرُ خِصَالٍ: حَتَّى يَكُونَ الرُّشْدُ مِنْهُ مَأْمُولًا، وَالْكِبْرُ مِنْهُ مَأْمُونًا، وَحَتَّى يَكُونَ الذُّلُّ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْعِزِّ، وحَتَّى يَكُونَ الْفَقْرُ أَحَبَّ إلَيْهِ مِنَ الْغِنَى، وحَتَّى يَسْتَقِلَّ مِنَ الْغِنَى، وَحَتَّى يَسْتَقِلَّ كَثِيرَ الْمَعْرُوفِ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ، ويْسِتَكْثِرَ قَلِيلَهُ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ، وَلَا يَتَبَرَّمَ بِمَنْ طَلَبَ إِلَيْهِ الْحَوَائِجَ، وَلَا يَسْأَمَ مِنْ طَلَبِ الْعِلْمِ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ شَيْءٌ، وَحَتَّى يَكُونَ الْقُوتُ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ، وَالْعَاشِرَةُ وَمَا الْعَاشِرَةُ بِهَا سَادَ مَجْدُهُ، وَعَلَا ذِكْرُهُ، يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ فَلَا يَرَى أَحَدًا مِنَ النَّاسِ إِلَّا ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ دُونَهُ "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us. He said: It reached me from Wahb b. Munabbih, who said:
records.matn_en: “God has not been worshipped with the like of reason (ʿaql), and a servant will not reach the reality of faith until ten qualities are in him: until rectitude is hoped for from him and arrogance is not feared from him; until humility is dearer to him than honor; until poverty is dearer to him than wealth; until he deems [his] wealth little; until he deems the abundant good he does little and deems the little good of others abundant; until he is not irritated by one who asks him for his needs; until he does not weary of seeking knowledge as long as any of his life remains; and until subsistence is dearer to him than surplus. And the tenth—and what is the tenth!—by which his glory is raised and his mention exalted: he goes out from his house and sees none of the people but he thinks that he is better than himself.”
translator_notes: The chain contains a break (‘it reached me from Wahb’). The source repeats the phrase ‘until he deems [wealth] little’ (wa-ḥattā yastaqilla mina al-ghinā) twice, apparently by dittography; it is rendered once, which brings the listed qualities to nine plus ‘the tenth’. The tenth quality, as printed, is that he sees no one without thinking himself beneath him.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The prohibition of plunder (al-nuhba)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي مَعْبَدٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «مَنِ انْتَهَبَ نُهْبَةً ذَاتَ شَرَفٍ يَرْفَعُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَنْظَارَهُمْ، فَلَيْسَ بِمُسْلِمٍ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr b. Dīnār, from Abū Maʿbad, who said:
records.matn_en: “Whoever plunders a prized plunder (nuhba dhāt sharaf) to which the Muslims raise their eyes is not a Muslim.”
translator_notes: Presented as Abū Maʿbad’s own statement, with no attribution to the Prophet or a Companion.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Lying is incompatible with faith
