records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ بَيَانٍ، وابْنِ أَبِي خَالِدٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازمٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقَ، يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ مُجَانِبٌ لِلْإِيمَانِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Bayān and Ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays b. Abī Ḥāzim, who said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq say:
records.matn_en: “O people, beware of lying, for lying is incompatible with faith.”

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا حُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْجُعْفِيُّ، عَنْ زَائِدَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا بَيَانٌ، عَنْ قَيْسٍ،
records.matn_ar: قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: «إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ مُجَانِبٌ لِلْإِيمَانِ»
records.isnad_en: Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī al-Juʿfī narrated to us, from Zāʾida. He said: Bayān narrated to us, from Qays. He said: Abū Bakr said:
records.matn_en: “Beware of lying, for lying is incompatible with faith.”

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا مَرْوَانُ بْنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ الْفَزَارِيُّ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنْ قَيْسٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقَ، يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: «إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ مُجَانِبٌ لِلْإِيمَانِ» . حَدَّثَنَا الْمِرْزِبَانُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ الْكِنْدِيُّ، عَنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنْ قَيْسٍ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ رحمه الله، مِثْلَهُ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ - أوْ هُوَ يَخْطُبُ
records.isnad_en: Marwān b. Muʿāwiya al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from Qays. He said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq say:
records.matn_en: “Beware of lying, for lying is incompatible with faith.” al-Mirzabān b. Masʿūd al-Kindī narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from Qays, from Abū Bakr (raḥimahu Allāh), the like of it, except that he said: I heard Abū Bakr saying—or: he was delivering a sermon.
translator_notes: The numbering passes from 55 to 57; no. 56 is not present in this export. A second chain (al-Mirzabān ← Ismāʿīl ← Qays ← Abū Bakr) follows within the same record.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Ablution is half of faith

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ جُرَيَّ النَّهْدِيَّ، يُحَدِّثُ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ بَنِي سُلَيْمٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: عَدَّهُنَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي يَدِي، قَالَ: «الْوُضُوءُ نِصْفُ الْإِيمَانِ، وَالصِّيَامُ نِصْفُ الصَّبْرِ، وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ نِصْفُ الْمِيزَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلَؤُهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ تَمْلَأُ مَا بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Yūnus b. Abī Isḥāq. He said: I heard Juray al-Nahdī narrate, from a man of Banū Sulaym, who said:
records.matn_en: The Messenger of God ﷺ counted them on my hand. He said: “Ablution is half of faith; fasting is half of patience; ‘Glory be to God’ is half of the scale; ‘Praise be to God’ fills it; and ‘God is greatest’ fills what is between heaven and earth.”
translator_notes: The Companion is an unnamed man of Banū Sulaym.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ: إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَوْسَطَ شَامِيٍّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: «اعْمَلُوا، وخَيْرُ أعْمَالِكُمُ الصَّلَاةُ، وَلَا يُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْوُضُوءِ إِلَّا مُؤْمِنٌ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, from a man called Ismāʿīl b. Awsaṭ, a Syrian, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Work, and the best of your works is the prayer, and none maintains ablution except a believer.”
translator_notes: Mursal: Ismāʿīl b. Awsaṭ does not name a Companion.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «مِنْ صِدْقِ الْإِيمَانِ وَبِرِّهِ إِسْبَاغُ الْوُضُوءِ فِي الْمَكَارِهِ، وَمِنْ صِدْقِ الْإِيمَانِ وَبِرِّهِ أَنْ يَخْلُوَ الرَّجُلُ بِالْمَرْأَةِ الْجَمِيلَةِ، فَيَدَعَهَا، لَا يَدَعُهَا إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عز وجل» . قَالَ سُفْيَانُ: وَعَدَّ أمُورًا مِنْ صِدْقِ الْإِيمَانِ وَبِرِّهِ
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us. He said: ʿAmr b. Dīnār narrated to us, from ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr, who said:
records.matn_en: “Among the truth of faith and its righteousness is performing ablution fully in times of hardship; and among the truth of faith and its righteousness is that a man be alone with a beautiful woman and leave her, leaving her for no reason but God, mighty and majestic.” Sufyān said: And he listed [other] matters from the truth of faith and its righteousness.
translator_notes: A saying of ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr, not attributed to the Prophet.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، عَنِ الْأَوْزَاعِيِّ، عَنْ حَسَّانِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.matn_ar: «وَالْوُضُوءُ شَطْرُ الْإِيمَانِ»
records.isnad_en: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Awzāʿī, from Ḥassān b. ʿAṭiyya, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “And ablution is half (shaṭr) of faith.”
translator_notes: Mursal: Ḥassān b. ʿAṭiyya does not name a Companion. The text begins with ‘and’, as printed.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ صَدَقَةَ مَوْلَى الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ أَبِي ثِفالٍ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ حُوَيْطِبٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: «لَا إِيمَانَ لِمَنْ لَا صَلَاةَ لَهُ، وَلَا صَلَاةَ لِمَنْ لَا وُضُوءَ لَهُ»
records.isnad_en: Wakīʿ narrated to us. He said: Ḥammād b. Salama narrated to us, from Ṣadaqa, freedman of al-Zubayr, from Abū Thifāl, from Abū Bakr b. Ḥuwayṭib, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “There is no faith for one who has no prayer, and no prayer for one who has no ablution.”
translator_notes: No Companion is named between Abū Bakr b. Ḥuwayṭib and the Prophet.

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on the application of the term ‘disbelief’ to one who abandons prayer
groups.title_ar: تَابِعْ بَابَ إِطْلَاقِ الْكُفْرِ عَلَى مَنْ تَرَكَ الصَّلَاةَ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا مَرْوَانُ الْفَزَارِيُّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي إِسْمَاعِيلَ السُّلَمِيُّ، عَنْ مَعْقِلٍ الْخَثْعَمِيِّ،، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: سَألَ رَجُلٌ ⦗ص: 127⦘ عَلِيًّا عَنِ امْرَأَةٍ لَا تُصَلِّي، فقَالَ عَلِيٌّ: «مَنْ لَمْ يُصَلِّ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ» قَالُوا: إِنَّهَا مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ، قَالَ: «تَتَّخِذُ صُوفَةً فِيهَا سَمْنٌ، أوْ زَيْتٌ، ثُمَّ تَغْتَسِلُ وتُصَلِّي»
records.isnad_en: Marwān al-Fazārī narrated to us. He said: Muḥammad b. Abī Ismāʿīl al-Sulamī narrated to us, from Maʿqil al-Khathʿamī, who said:
records.matn_en: A man asked [p. 127] ʿAlī about a woman who does not pray. ʿAlī said: “Whoever does not pray is a disbeliever.” They said: She has abnormal bleeding (mustaḥāḍa). He said: “She takes a piece of wool with ghee or oil on it, then bathes and prays.”
translator_notes: The source has a doubled comma after ‘al-Khathʿamī’, perhaps marking an omission.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Warning against harming the neighbor, and that it diminishes faith
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ التَّرْهِيبُ مِنْ أَذَى الْجَارِ وَأَنَّهُ يُنْقِصُ الْإِيمَانَ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا مَرْوَانُ الْفَزَارِيُّ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي الصَّبَّاحُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ مُرَّةَ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، حَدَّثَ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَسَمَ بَيْنَكُمْ أخْلَاقَكُمْ، كَمَا قَسَمَ بَيْنَكُمْ أرْزَاقَكُمْ، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُعْطِي عَلَى نِيَّةِ الدُّنْيَا مَنْ يُحِبُّ وَمَنْ لَا يُحِبُّ، وَلَا يُعْطِي الدِّينَ إِلَّا مَنْ يُحِبُّ، فَمَنْ أعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ الدِّينَ فَقَدْ أَحَبَّهُ، وَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ لَا يُسْلِمُ عَبْدٌ حَتَّى يَسْلَمَ قَلْبُهُ وَلِسَانُهُ، وَلَا يُؤْمِنُ حَتَّى يَأْمَنَ جَارُهُ بَوَائِقَهُ» قُلْنَا: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ وَمَا بَوَائِقُهُ؟ قَالَ: «غَشْمُهُ وَظُلْمُهُ، وَلَا يَكْسِبُ عَبْدٌ مالًا حَرَامًا، فَيُنْفِقَ مِنْهُ، فَيُبَارَكَ لَهُ فِيهِ، وَلَا يَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ فَيُتَقَبَّلَ مِنْهُ، وَلَا يَتْرُكُهُ خَلْفَ ظَهْرِهِ إِلَّا كَانَ زادَهُ إِلَى النَّارِ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ عز وجل لَا يَمْحُو السَّيِّئَ بِالسَّيِّئِ، وَلَكِنْ يَمْحُو السَّيِّئَ بِالْحَسَنِ، إِنَّ الْخَبِيثَ لَا يَمْحُوهُ الْخَبِيثُ»
records.isnad_en: Marwān al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Abān b. Isḥāq. He said: al-Ṣabbāḥ b. Muḥammad narrated to me, from Murra al-Hamdānī, that ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd narrated that he heard the Prophet of God ﷺ say:
records.matn_en: “God has apportioned among you your characters as He has apportioned among you your provisions. God gives the world, according to the intention of the world (ʿalā niyyat al-dunyā), to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, but He gives religion only to whom He loves; so whoever God gives religion, He has loved him. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, no servant is a Muslim until his heart and his tongue are safe, and none believes until his neighbor is safe from his harms (bawāʾiq).” We said: O Prophet of God, what are his harms? He said: “His violence and his wrongdoing. And no servant earns unlawful wealth and spends from it, and it is blessed for him in it; nor does he give it in charity and have it accepted from him; nor does he leave it behind his back, but that it is his provision to the Fire. Indeed, God, mighty and majestic, does not wipe out evil with evil, but wipes out evil with good. Indeed, the foul is not wiped out by the foul.”
translator_notes: The phrase ‘ʿalā niyyat al-dunyā’ (lit. ‘on the intention of the world’) is obscure; it is rendered literally.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The obligation of loyalty for God’s sake and enmity for God’s sake
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ وُجُوبُ الْمُوالَاةِ فِي اللَّهِ وَالْبُغْضِ فِي اللَّهِ

records.isnad_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْجُعْفِيُّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا زَائِدَةُ بْنُ قُدَامَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا لَيْثُ بْنُ أَبِي سُلَيْمٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «أَحِبَّ فِي اللَّهِ، وَأَبْغِضْ فِي اللَّهِ، وَوَالِ فِي اللَّهِ، وَعَادِ فِي اللَّهِ، فَإِنَّمَا تُنَالُ مُوالَاةُ اللَّهِ بذَلِكَ، وَلَنْ يَجِدَ عَبْدٌ طَعْمَ الْإِيمَانِ وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ صَلَاتُهُ وَصَوْمُهُ حَتَّى يَكُونَ كَذَلِكَ، ولَقَدْ صَارَتْ عَامَّةُ مُؤَاخَاةِ النَّاسِ عَلَى أَمْرِ الدُّنْيَا، وذَلِكَ لَا يُجْدِي عَنْ أَهْلِهِ» . ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ هاتَيْنِ الآيَتَيْنِ: {لَا تَجِدُ قَوْمًا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ} [المجادلة: 22] الْمُجَادَلَةُ وَقَرَأَ {الْأَخِلَّاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ} [الزخرف: 67] الزُّخْرُفُ الْآيَةَ
records.isnad_en: al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī al-Juʿfī informed us. He said: Zāʾida b. Qudāma narrated to us. He said: Layth b. Abī Sulaym narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said:
records.matn_en: “Love for God’s sake, hate for God’s sake, befriend for God’s sake, and be hostile for God’s sake, for the friendship of God is attained only by that; and a servant will never taste the sweetness of faith, however much his prayer and fasting, until he is thus. Indeed, most of the fraternity of people has come to be over worldly matters, and that avails its people nothing.” Then Ibn ʿAbbās recited these two verses: “You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day” [Q. 58:22] (al-Mujādila); and he recited “Friends on that Day will be, to one another, enemies” [Q. 43:67] (al-Zukhruf)—the verse.
translator_notes: No number is printed in the source; by sequence it would be no. 65 (the preceding narration is 64 and the next is 66).

groups.title_en: Chapter: The passing away of knowledge

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، يَقُولُ:
records.matn_ar: «هَلْ يُدْرَى كَيْفَ يَنْقُصُ الْإِسْلَامُ؟» قَالُوا: كَيْفَ؟ قَالَ: «كَمَا تُنْقِصُ الدَّابَّةَ سَمْنَهَا، وَكَمَا يَنْقُصُ الثَّوْبُ عَنْ طُولِ اللُّبْسِ، وَكَمَا يَقْسُو الدِّرْهَمُ عَنْ طُولِ الْخَبْوِ، وَقَدْ يَكُونُ فِي الْقَبِيلَةِ عالِمَانِ، فيَمُوتُ أحَدُهُمَا فَيَذْهَبُ نِصْفُ عِلْمِهِ، ويَمُوتُ الْآخَرُ فَيَذْهَبُ عِلْمُهُمْ كُلُّهُ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say:
records.matn_en: “Do you know how Islam diminishes?” They said: How? He said: “As an animal loses its fat, and as a garment wears thin from long use, and as a dirham hardens from long hoarding (khabw). And there may be in a tribe two scholars; one of them dies and half of his knowledge goes, and the other dies and all of their knowledge goes.”
translator_notes: The expression ‘yaqsū al-dirham ʿan ṭūl al-khabw’ is rare and the rendering is tentative. The antecedent of ‘his knowledge’ is not clear in the source.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Legal obligations (al-takālīf al-sharʿiyya) are part of faith

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ هَارُونَ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ حُسَيْنٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ الرَّحَبِيِّ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: سُئِلَ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، مَقْبِلَهُ مِنَ الشَّامِ عَنْ خِصَالٍ عَنِ الْإِيمَانِ، فَتَلَا هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ {لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ} [البقرة: 177] الْآيَةَ
records.isnad_en: Yazīd b. Hārūn narrated to us. He said: Sufyān b. Ḥusayn informed us, from Abū ʿAlī al-Raḥabī, from ʿIkrima, who said:
records.matn_en: Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī was asked, on his return from Syria, about the qualities of faith, and he recited this verse: “Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east and the west” [Q. 2:177]—the verse.
translator_notes: The report is given as an event narrated by ʿIkrima without naming a source; the verse is cited in abbreviated form (‘the verse’).

groups.title_en: Chapter: The description of the Muslim

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي خَالِدٍ، سَمِعَهُ مِنَ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: وَحَدَّثَنَا دَاوُدُ بْنُ أَبِي هِنْدٍ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ يَتَخَلَّلُ حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، قَالَ: وَحَدَّثَ فِي مكَانٍ آخَرَ يَتَخَطَّى رِقَابَ النَّاسِ فقَالَ: أَخْبِرْنِي بِشَيْءٍ سَمِعْتَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، قَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي عُمَرَ: وَوَجَدْتُ فِي مكَانٍ آخَرَ: حَدِّثْنِي بِحَدِيثٍ سَمِعْتَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَلَا تُحَدِّثْنِي عَنِ الْعِدْلَيْنِ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ: «الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ، وَالْمُهَاجِرُ مَنْ هَجَرَ مَا حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Khālid, who heard it from al-Shaʿbī. He said: And Dāwūd b. Abī Hind narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:
records.matn_en: A man came, picking his way through [the people] until he reached ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr—and he narrated in another place that he came stepping over the necks of the people—and said: Tell me something you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Ibn Abī ʿUmar said: And I found in another place: Narrate to me a ḥadīth that you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ, and do not narrate to me from the two loads (al-ʿidlayn). He said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe, and the emigrant is one who abandons what God has forbidden him.”
translator_notes: ‘Ibn Abī ʿUmar said’ is the compiler adding a variant wording he found elsewhere. The meaning of ‘the two loads’ (al-ʿidlayn) is not explained in the source and is rendered literally.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Religion is sincere advice (naṣīḥa)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ اللَّيْثِيِّ، عَنْ تَمِيمٍ الدَّارِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم:
records.matn_ar: «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ، الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ، الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ» قَالَ: قُلْنَا: لِمَنْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: «للَّهِ ولِرَسُولِهِ، ولِصَالِحِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَلِكِتابِهِ، ولِأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Suhayl b. Abī Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAṭāʾ b. Yazīd al-Laythī, from Tamīm al-Dārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “Religion is sincere advice; religion is sincere advice; religion is sincere advice.” He said: We said: For whom, O Messenger of God? He said: “For God, for His Messenger, for the righteous among the believers, for His Book, and for the leaders of the Muslims.”

groups.title_en: Chapter: The most excellent of people in faith are the most excellent of them in knowledge (maʿrifa)
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ أفْضَلُ النَّاسِ إِيمَانًا أفْضَلُهُمْ مَعْرِفَةً

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا كُوفِيٌّ لَنَا - أوْ كُوفُيُّونَ -، عَنْ أَبِي السَّوْدَاءِ، عَنِ ابْنِ سَابِطٍ، رِوَايَةً قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «أَفْضَلُكُمْ إِيمَانًا أَفْضَلُكُمْ مَعْرِفَةً»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna narrated to us. He said: A Kūfan of ours—or Kūfans—narrated to us, from Abū al-Sawdāʾ, from Ibn Sābiṭ, as a transmitted report (riwāyatan). He said:
records.matn_en: “The most excellent of you in faith are the most excellent of you in knowledge.”
translator_notes: Sufyān is unsure whether he heard it from one Kūfan or from several, and none is named. The word ‘riwāyatan’ is as printed; the source does not state whom the saying is attributed to.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعْدٍ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: " مَا زَالَتِ الْخُصُومَةُ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى خَاصَمَ الرُّوحُ الْجَسَدَ، فقَالَ الْجَسَدُ: يَا رَبِّ إِنَّمَا كُنْتُ مِثْلَ الْخَشَبَةِ النَّخِرَةِ، لَيْسَ لِي يَدٌ أَبْطُشُ بِهَا، وَلَا عَيْنٌ أُبْصِرُ بِهَا، وَلَا أُذُنٌ أسْمَعُ بِهَا، وَلَا رِجْلٌ أمْشِي بِهَا، وَلَا عَقْلٌ أَعْقِلُ بِهِ، حَتَّى جَاءَ هَذَا فَدَخَلَ فِيَّ، فَنَجِّنِي مِنْهُ، وخَلِّدْ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذَابَ الْيَوْمَ. وقَالَ الرُّوحُ: يَا رَبِّ مِنْكَ الرُّوحُ وَأَنْتَ خَلَقْتَهُ، إِنَّمَا كُنْتُ كَالشِّهَابِ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِي يَدٌ أَبْطِشُ بِهَا، وَلَا عَيْنٌ أُبْصِرُ بِهَا، وَلَا أُذُنٌ أسْمَعُ بِهَا، وَلَا رِجْلٌ أَمْشِي بِهَا، وَلَا عَقْلٌ أَعْقِلُ بِهِ، حَتَّى جِئْتُ فَدُخِّلْتُ فِي هَذَا الْجَسَدِ، فَخَلِّدْ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذَابَ وَنَجِّنِي مِنْهُ الْيَوْمَ، فَقِيلَ: يُضْرَبُ لَكُمَا مَثَلٌ مَثَلُكُمَا كَمَثَلِ أَعْمَى ومُقْعَدٍ، دَخَلَا حَائِطًا دَانِيَةً ثِمَارُهَا، فَالْأَعْمَى لَا يُبْصِرُ الثِّمَارَ فَيَتَنَاوَلَ مِنْهَا، وَالْمُقْعَدُ يُبْصِرُهَا وَلَا يَنَالُهَا، فَدَعَا الْمُقْعَدُ الْأَعْمَى، فقَالَ: احْمِلْنِي حَتَّى أُسَدِّدَكَ، فَآكُلَ وأُطْعِمَكَ، فَحَمَلَهُ وَسَدَّدَهُ، فَأَدْرَكَا وَهُمَا كَذَلِكَ، فعَلَى أيِّهِمَا يَقَعُ الْعَذَابُ؟ قَالَ: عَلَيْهِمَا جَمِيعًا، قَالَ: فَالْعَذَابُ عَلَيْهِمَا "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Saʿd, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
records.matn_en: “Disputation among people will not cease on the Day of Resurrection until the spirit disputes with the body. The body will say: My Lord, I was only like a rotten log; I had no hand with which to strike, no eye with which to see, no ear with which to hear, no foot with which to walk, and no mind with which to reason, until this one came and entered me. So save me from it and make the punishment on it eternal today. And the spirit will say: My Lord, from You is the spirit, and You created it; I was only like a flame, having no hand with which to strike, no eye with which to see, no ear with which to hear, no foot with which to walk, and no mind with which to reason, until I came and was made to enter this body. So make the punishment on it eternal, and save me from it today. Then it will be said: A parable is struck for you both: your parable is that of a blind man and a lame man who entered an orchard whose fruits hung low; the blind man cannot see the fruits to take from them, and the lame man sees them but cannot reach them. The lame man called the blind man and said: Carry me so that I may guide you aright, so that I may eat and feed you. So he carried him and guided him, and they reached [the fruit] while they were thus. Upon which of them will the punishment fall? He said: Upon both of them together. He said: So the punishment is upon both of them.”
translator_notes: The question ‘Upon which of them will the punishment fall?’ and its answer are part of the parable; the person who answers is not named in the source. ‘Abū Saʿd’ is not further identified.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The sin of one who withholds zakāt

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: " مَا مِنْ صَاحِبِ إِبِلٍ لَا يُؤَدِّي حَقَّهَا، وَمِنْ حَقِّهَا حَلْبُهَا يَوْمَ وِرْدِهَا إِلَّا بُطِحَ لَهَا بِقَاعٍ أوْ بِصَعِيدٍ قَرْقَرٍ، فَتَسْتَنُّ عَلَيْهِ، تَطَؤُهُ بِأَخْفَافِهَا كُلَّمَا مَضَى آخِرُهَا رُدَّ عَلَيْهِ أَوَّلُهَا. وَمَا مِنْ صَاحِبِ بَقَرٍ لَا يُؤَدِّي حَقَّهَا وَمِنْ حَقِّهَا حَلْبُهَا يَوْمَ وِرْدِهَا إِلَّا بُطِحَ لَهَا بِقَاعٍ أوْ بِصَعِيدٍ قَرْقَرٍ، فَتَسْتَنُّ تَطَؤُهُ بِأَظْلَافِهَا، وتَنْطَحُهُ بِقُرُونِهَا كُلَّمَا مَضَى آخِرُهَا رُدَّ أَوَّلُهَا. وَمَا مِنْ صَاحِبِ غَنَمٍ لَا يُؤَدِّي حَقَّهَا، وَمِنْ حَقِّهَا حَلْبُهَا يَوْمَ وِرْدِهَا إِلَّا بُطِحَ لَهَا بِقَاعٍ أوْ بِصَعِيدٍ قَرْقَرٍ تَطؤُهُ بِأَظْلَافِهَا وتَنْطَحُهُ بِقُرُونِهَا لَيْسَ فِيهَا جَمَّاءُ، وَلَا مَكْسُورَةُ الْقَرْنِ. وَمَا مِنْ صَاحِبِ كَنْزٍ لَا يُؤَدِّي زَكَاتَهُ إِلَّا مُثِّلَ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شُجَاعٌ أَقْرَعُ فاغِرًا فَاهُ، يَطْلُبُهُ وَهُوَ يَفِرُّ مِنْهُ، ويَقُولُ: أنَا كَنْزُكَ الَّذِي خَبَّأْتَهُ، وَلَا يَنْتَهِي حَتَّى يَضَعَ يَدَهُ فِي فِيهِ "
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr b. Dīnār, from ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “There is no owner of camels who does not pay their due—and part of their due is milking them on the day they come to water—but that he will be laid out for them in a level plain or on smooth, bare ground, and they will tread on him with their feet; whenever the last of them has passed, the first of them is brought back upon him. And there is no owner of cattle who does not pay their due—and part of their due is milking them on the day they come to water—but that he will be laid out for them in a level plain or on smooth, bare ground, and they will trample him with their cloven hooves and gore him with their horns; whenever the last of them has passed, the first of them is brought back. And there is no owner of sheep who does not pay their due—and part of their due is milking them on the day they come to water—but that he will be laid out for them in a level plain or on smooth, bare ground, and they will trample him with their cloven hooves and gore him with their horns; there will be none among them hornless or with a broken horn. And there is no owner of a treasure who does not pay its zakāt but that there will be made to appear to him on the Day of Resurrection a bald serpent with its mouth open, pursuing him while he flees from it, saying: I am your treasure that you hoarded; and it will not stop until it puts his hand in its mouth.”
translator_notes: Mursal: ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr does not name a Companion.

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ أعْيَنَ، وجَامِعِ بْنِ أَبِي رَاشِدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، يَبْلُغُ بِهِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ لَا يُؤَدِّي زَكَاةَ مَالِهِ إِلَّا جُعِلَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِي عُنُقِهِ شُجَاعٌ» ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَيْنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُصَادِقَهُ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: {وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ} الْآيَةَ. وقَالَ مَرَّةً: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَيْنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِصْدَاقَهُ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: {سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ} [آل عمران: 180] الْآيَةَ
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik b. Aʿyan and Jāmiʿ b. Abī Rāshid, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd (r), reaching the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
records.matn_en: “There is no man who does not pay the zakāt of his wealth but that on the Day of Resurrection a serpent will be placed around his neck.” Then the Messenger of God ﷺ recited to us its confirmation from the Book of God: “And let not those who are miserly with what God has given them of His bounty think…” [the verse]. And on another occasion he said: Then the Messenger of God ﷺ recited to us its confirmation from the Book of God: “They will be collared with what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection” [Q. 3:180]—the verse.
translator_notes: ‘Reaching the Prophet’ (yablughu bihi) is the source’s formula for the report’s attribution. The source gives two spellings of ‘its confirmation’ (muṣādiqahu / miṣdāqahu) across the two citations; only the second citation carries the verse reference [Q. 3:180].

groups.title_en: Chapter: Mention of the Khawārij and their attributes

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُعَاذٍ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: بَيْنَمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ يَقْسِمُ قَسْمًا إِذْ جَاءَهُ ابْنُ ذِي الْخُوَيْصِرَةِ التَّمِيمِيُّ، فقَالَ: اعْدِلْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّكَ لَمْ تَعْدِلْ. قَالَ: «وَيْلَكَ فَمَنْ يَعْدِلُ إِذَا لَمْ أَعْدِلْ» قَالَ عُمَرُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ائْذَنْ لِي فَأَضْرِبْ عُنُقَهُ، قَالَ: " دَعْهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ أَصْحَابًا يَحْتَقِرُ أحَدُكُمْ صَلَاتَهُ مَعَ صَلَاتِهِمْ وَصِيَامَهُ مَعَ صِيَامِهِمْ، يَقْرَءُونَ الْقُرْآنَ لَا يُجَاوِزُ ⦗ص: 138⦘ تَرَاقِيَهُمْ يَمْرُقُونَ مِنَ الدِّينِ كَمَا يَمْرُقُ السَّهْمُ مِنَ الرَّمِيَّةِ يُنْظَرُ فِي قُذَذِهِ فَلَا يُوجَدُ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ، ثُمَّ يُنْظَرُ فِي نَضِيِّهِ فَلَا يُوجَدُ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ، ثُمَّ يُنْظَرُ فِي رِصَافِهِ فَلَا يُوجَدُ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ، ثُمَّ يُنْظَرُ فِي نَصْلِهِ فَلَا يَجِدُ فِيهِ شَيْئًا قَدْ سَبَقَ الْفَرْثَ الدَّمُ آيَتُهُمْ رَجُلٌ أسْوَدُ إِحْدَى يَدَيْهِ مِثْلُ ثَدْيِ الْمَرْأَةِ أوْ مِثْلُ الْبَضْعَةِ تَدَرْدَرُ يَخْرُجُونَ عَلَى فُرْقَةٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ قَالَ: وفِيهِمْ نَزَلَتْ {ومِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُلْمِزُكَ فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ} [التوبة: 58] التَّوْبَةُ. قَالَ أَبُو سَعِيدٍ: أَشْهَدُ أنِّي سَمِعْتُ هَذَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، وأشْهَدُ أَنَّ عَلِيًّا حِينَ قَتَلَهُمْ وأنَا مَعهُ جِيءَ بِالرَّجُلِ عَلَى النَّعْتِ الَّذِي نَعَتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
records.isnad_en: ʿAbd Allāh b. Muʿādh narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said:
records.matn_en: While the Messenger of God was distributing a portion, Ibn Dhī al-Khuwayṣira al-Tamīmī came to him and said: Be just, O Messenger of God, for you have not been just. He said: “Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just?” ʿUmar said: O Messenger of God, permit me to strike off his neck. He said: “Leave him, for he has companions: one of you will think his prayer small beside their prayer and his fasting small beside their fasting. They recite the Qurʾān but it does not pass [p. 138] their collarbones; they pass out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the quarry: [the archer] looks at its fletching (qudhadh) and finds nothing in it; then he looks at its shaft (naḍiyy) and finds nothing in it; then he looks at its binding (riṣāf) and finds nothing in it; then he looks at its head (naṣl) and finds nothing in it—the blood has outstripped the dung. Their sign is a black man, one of whose arms is like a woman’s breast, or like a piece of flesh, quivering. They will emerge at a time of division among the people.” He said: And about them was revealed {And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities} [Q. 9:58] (al-Tawba). Abū Saʿīd said: I testify that I heard this from the Messenger of God, and I testify that ʿAlī, when he fought them, while I was with him, had the man brought, in the very description that the Messenger of God had described.
translator_notes: No number is printed for this narration; the number 74 is printed with the preceding heading. The source prints no honorific after ‘the Messenger of God’ in this report. The quotation opened before ‘Leave him’ is not closed in the source. The wording ‘the blood has outstripped the dung’ (sabaqa al-farth al-damu) is as printed; the usual wording of this simile is that the arrow ‘outstripped the dung and the blood’.

groups.title_en: Chapter: Which Islam is best?

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا الْمُقْرِئُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْمَسْعُودِيُّ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ، عَنْ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ الزَبِيدِيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ نَادَاهُ رَجُلٌ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أيُّ الْإِسْلَامِ أفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «أَنْ يَسْلَمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِكَ وَيَدِكَ»
records.isnad_en: al-Muqriʾ narrated to us. He said: al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from ʿAmr b. Murra, from ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith, from Abū Kathīr al-Zubaydī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ, from the Prophet ﷺ, that
records.matn_en: a man called out to him: O Messenger of God, which Islam is best? He said: “That the Muslims be safe from your tongue and your hand.”

narrators.en: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ

groups.title_en: Chapter: The call to the two testimonies and the laws (sharāʾiʿ) of Islam
groups.title_ar: بَابٌ الدُّعَاءُ إِلَى الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ وَشَرَائِعِ الْإِسْلَامِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ السُّرِّيِّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا زَكَرِيَّا بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ صَيْفِيٍّ، عَنْ أَبِي مَعْبَدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَعَثَ مُعَاذَ بْنَ جَبَلٍ إِلَى الْيَمَنِ، فقَالَ: «إِنَّكَ سَتَأْتِي قَوْمًا أَهْلَ كِتَابٍ، فَإِذَا أَتَيْتَهُمْ فَادْعُهُمْ إِلَى أَنْ يَشْهَدُوا أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، فَإِنْ هُمْ أطَاعُوكَ بذَلِكَ فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ خَمْسَ صَلَوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ، فَإِنْ هُمْ أَطَاعُوا لَكَ بذَلِكَ فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُؤْخَذُ مِنْ أَغْنِيَائِهِمْ فَتُرَدُّ عَلَى فُقَرَائِهِمْ، فَإِنْ هُمْ أَطَاعُوا لَكَ بِذَلِكَ فَإِيِّاكَ وَكَرَائِمَ أَمْوَالِهِمْ. وَاتَّقِ دَعْوَةَ الْمَظْلُومِ، فَإِنَّهَا لَيْسَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ اللَّهِ عز وجل حِجَابٌ»
records.isnad_en: Bishr b. al-Sarī narrated to us. He said: Zakariyyā b. Isḥāq narrated to us, from Yaḥyā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣayfī, from Abū Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ
records.matn_en: sent Muʿādh b. Jabal to Yemen and said: “You will come to a people, People of the Book. When you come to them, call them to testify that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God. If they obey you in that, inform them that five prayers are obligatory upon them in a day and a night. If they obey you in that, inform them that a charity (ṣadaqa) is obligatory upon them, to be taken from their rich and returned to their poor. If they obey you in that, then beware of the choicest of their wealth. And beware the supplication of the wronged, for between it and God, mighty and majestic, there is no veil.”

narrators.en: Yaḥyā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣayfī

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on the departure of faith upon committing acts of disobedience
groups.title_ar: تَابِعْ بَابَ زَوَالِ الْإِيمَانِ عِنْدَ ارْتِكَابِ الْمَعَاصِي

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الْأَعْرَجِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: «لَا يَشْرَبُ رَجُلٌ الْخَمْرَ حِينَ يَشْرَبُهَا وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ»
records.isnad_en: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said:
records.matn_en: “A man does not drink wine, at the time he drinks it, while he is a believer.”

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on the call to the two testimonies and the laws of Islam
groups.title_ar: تَابِعْ بَابَ الدُّعَاءِ إِلَى الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ وَشَرَائِعِ الْإِسْلَامِ

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ حَمَّادُ بْنُ أُسَامَةَ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: الْمُجَالِدُ، أَخْبَرَنَا ذَلِكَ، قَالَ: كَتَبَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى جَدِّي وَهَذَا كِتَابُهُ عِنْدَنَا، وحَدَّثَنِي ذَلِكَ أشْيَاخُ الْحَيِّ، " بسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ، مِنْ مُحَمَّدٍ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ إِلَى عُمَيْرٍ ذِي مُرَّانَ وَإِلَى مَنْ أَسْلَمَ مِنْ هَمْدَانَ، سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ، إِنِّي أَحْمَدُ إِلَيْكُمُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ. أَمَّا بَعْدُ: فَإِنَّهُ بَلَغَنَا إسْلَامُكُمْ مَرْجِعَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِ الرُّومِ، فَأَبْشِرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ هَدَاكُمْ بِهُدَاهُ، وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذَا شَهِدْتُمْ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَأَقَمْتُمُ الصَّلَاةَ، وَأَنْطَيْتُمُ الزَّكَاةَ، فَإِنَّ لَكُمْ ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ، وَذِمَّةَ مُحَمَّدٍ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، عَلَى أمْوالِكُمْ وَدِمَائِكُمْ وَأرْضِ الْبُورِ الَّتِي أسْلَمْتُمْ عَلَيْهَا، سَهْلِهَا وَجَبَلِهَا ومَرَاعِيهَا وَغُيُولِهَا، غَيْرَ مَظْلُومِينَ ومُضَيَّقٍ عَلَيْهِمْ "
records.isnad_en: Abū Usāma Ḥammād b. Usāma narrated to us. He said: al-Mujālid informed us of that. He said:
records.matn_en: The Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to my grandfather, and this letter of his is with us, and the elders of the tribe narrated it to me: “In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. From Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, to ʿUmayr Dhū Murrān and to those of Hamdān who have embraced Islam: Peace be upon you. I praise to you God, besides whom there is no god. To proceed: It has reached us that you have embraced Islam, on our return from the land of the Romans. So rejoice, for God has guided you with His guidance. And if you bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, and you establish the prayer and give (anṭaytum) the zakāt, then you have the protection of God and the protection of Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, over your wealth and your blood and the barren land (arḍ al-būr) on which you embraced Islam—its plain and its mountain, its pastures and its streams (ghuyūl)—not wronged and not constrained.”
translator_notes: The speaker of ‘my grandfather’ is presumably al-Mujālid (of Hamdān); the source does not say so explicitly. ‘Anṭaytum’ is a dialectal variant of ‘aʿṭaytum’ (‘you give’). The words ‘arḍ al-būr’ and ‘ghuyūl’ are rare and the rendering is tentative.

groups.title_en: Chapter: The dislike of assuming leadership (imāra)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ عِيسَى الرَّمْلِيُّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ طَارِقِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ رَافِعِ بْنِ أَبِي رَافِعٍ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ: إِنِّي اخْتَرْتُكَ لِنَفْسِي فَعَلِّمْنِي شَيْئًا آخُذُ بِهِ، قَالَ: قَدْ أرَدْتَ ذَلِكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقُولَ لِي: «تَعْبُدَ اللَّهِ وَلَا تُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَتُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِيَ الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وَلَا تَأَمَّرَ عَلَى رَجُلَيْنِ»
records.isnad_en: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā al-Ramlī narrated to us. He said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Sulaymān b. Maysara, from Ṭāriq b. Shihāb, from Rāfiʿ b. Abī Rāfiʿ, who said:
records.matn_en: I said to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq: I have chosen you for myself, so teach me something to hold to. He said: You had wished for that before you said it to me: “You worship God and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give the zakāt, fast Ramaḍān, and do not take command over two men.”
translator_notes: The source reads ‘araddta’ (‘you had wished’) where ‘aradtu’ (‘I had wished’) might be expected from the sense; it is rendered as printed.

groups.title_en: Continuation of the chapter on following the Sunna

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَاحِدِ بْنُ أيْمَنَ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: كَانَ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ، يَأْمُرَ: " أَنْ أَقْرَأَ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ عَلَى النَّاسِ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ: فَإِنَّا نُوصِيكُمْ بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ، وَنَحُثُّكُمْ عَلَى أَمْرِهِ، ونَرْضَى لَكُمْ طَاعَتَهُ، ونَسْخَطُ لَكُمْ مَعْصِيَتَهُ، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ الْكِتَابَ بِعِلْمِهِ فَأَحْكَمَهُ، وَفَصَّلَهُ وأَعَزَّهُ، وحَفِظَهُ أَنْ يَأتِيَهُ الْبَاطِلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ، وضَرَبَ ⦗ص: 146⦘ أمْثَالَهُ، وَبَيَّنَ عِبَرَهُ، وَجَعَلَهُ فُرْقَانًا مِنَ الشَّرِ، ونُورًا مِنَ الظُّلْمَةِ، وَبَصَرًا مِنَ الْعَمَى، وهُدًى مِنَ الضَّلَالَةِ، ثُمَّ تَمَّتِ النِعْمَةُ، وأُكْمِلَتِ الْعِبَادَةُ، وَحُفِظَتِ الْوَصِيَّةُ، وَجَرَتِ السُّنَّةُ وَمَضَتِ الْمَوْعِظَةُ، واعْتَقَدَ الْمِيثَاقُ، واسْتُوجِبَتِ الطَّاعَةُ، فَهُوَ حَبْلُ اللَّهِ الْمَتِينُ، وَالْعُرْوَةُ الْوُثْقَى لَا انْفِصَامَ لَهَا، بِهَا سَبَقَ الْأَوَّلُونَ، وَبِهَا أَدْرَكَ الْآخِرُونَ، كِتَابًا تَوَلَّى حُكْمَهُ، وارْتَضَاهُ لِنَفْسِهِ، وافْتَرَضَهُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ، مَنْ حَفِظَهُ بَلَّغَهُ مَا سِوَاهُ، ومَنْ ضَيَّعَهُ لَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهُ غَيْرُهُ، أَمَّا بَعْدُ: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تبارك وتعالى أَنْزَلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ النُّبُوَّةَ، وابْتَعَثَهُ بِالرِّسَالَةِ، رَحْمَةً لِلنَّاسِ كَافَّةً، وَالنَّاسُ حِينَئِذٍ فِي ظُلْمَةِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ وضَالَّتِهَا، يَعْبُدُونَ أوْثَانَهَا، وَيَسْتَقْسِمُونَ بَأَزْلَامِهَا، عَنْهَا يَأْتَمِرُونَ أمْرَهُمْ، وَبِهَا يُحِلُّونَ حَلَالَهُمْ، وَيُحَرِّمُونَ حَرَامَهُمْ، دِينُهُمْ بِدْعَةٌ، وَدَعْوَتُهُمْ فِرْيَةٌ، فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ عز وجل بِالْحَقِ مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم، رَحْمَةً مِنْهُ لَكُمْ ومِنَّةً مَنَّ بِهَا عَلَيْكُمْ، وبَشَّرَكُمْ وأَنْذَرَكُمْ ذِكْرَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْأُمَمِ، وَقَصَّ فِي الْكِتَابِ قِصَّةَ أمْرِهِمْ، كَيْفَ نَصَحَتْ لَهُمْ رَسُلُهُمْ، وكَيْفَ كَذَّبُوهُمْ وتَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُمْ، وكَيْفَ كَانَتْ عُقُوبَةُ اللَّهِ إيَّاهُمْ، فَوَعَظَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِنَكَالِ مَنْ قَبْلَكُمْ، وأمَرَكُمْ أَنْ تَقْتَدُوا بِصَالِحِ فِعَالِهِمْ، فَبَلَّغَ مُحَمَّدٌ الرِّسَالَةَ، وَنَصَحَ الْأُمَّةَ، وَعَمِلَ بِالطَّاعَةِ، وجَاهَدَ الْعَدُوَّ، فَأعَزَّ اللَّهُ بِهِ أمْرَهُ، وأظْهَرَ بِهِ نُورَهُ، وتَمَّتْ بِهِ كَلِمَتُهُ، وانْتَجَبَ لَهُ أقْوَامًا عَرِفُوا حقَّ اللَّهِ، واعْتَرَفُوا بِهِ، وبَذَلُوا لَهُ دِمَاءَهُمْ وأمْوَالَهُمْ، فِيهِمْ مَنْ هَجَرَ دَارَهُ وعَشِيرَتَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ عز وجل، ومِنْهُمْ آوَى ونَصَرَ فآسَوْا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَآسَوْا بِهِ. وَلَمْ يرْغَبُوا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ، فأيَّدَ اللَّهُ بِهِمُ الدِّينَ، ودَمَغَ الْحَقُّ ⦗ص: 147⦘ الْبَاطِلَ، وأُبْطِلَتْ دَعْوَةُ الطَّوَاغِيتِ، وَكُسِرَتِ الْأَزْلَامُ، وتُرِكَتْ عِبَادَةُ الْأَوْثَانِ، وَأُجِيبَ دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ وظَهَرَ دِينُ اللَّهِ، وَعَرَفَ النَّاسُ أَمْرَ اللَّهِ عز وجل، واعْتَرَفُوا بِقَضَاءِ اللَّهِ، وَشَهِدُوا بِالْحَقِّ، وَقَالُوا لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وأدَّوْا فَرَائِضَ اللَّهِ عز وجل، وأَعْقَبَ اللَّهِ نَبِيَّهُ مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم وَمَنِ اسْتَجَابَ لَهُ أجْرًا ونَصْرًا وَوَعْدًا وَسُلْطَانًا، وَمَكَّنَ لَهُمْ دِينَهُمُ الَّذِي ارْتَضَى، وأَبْدَلَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ خَوفِهِمْ أمْنًا، فَلَمَّا أحْكَمَ اللَّهِ النَّهْيَ عَنْ مَعْصِيَتِهِ، وَخَلُصَتِ الدَّعْوَةُ، وايْتَطَى الْإِسْلَامُ لِأَهْلِهِ، شَرَّعَ الدِّينَ شَرَائِعَهُ، وفَرَضَ فَرَائِضَهُ، وأعْلَمَ الدِّينَ عَلَامَةً يَعْلَمُهَا أَهْلُ الْإِسْلَامِ، وَحَدَّ الْحُدُودَ وَحَرَّمَ الْمَشَاعِرَ وَعَلَّمَ الْمَنَاسِكَ، وَمَضَتِ السُّنَّةُ، واسْتَتَابَ الْمُذْنِبَ، ودَعَا إِلَى الْهِجْرَةِ، وَفَتَحَ بَابَ التَّوْبَةِ، حُجَّةً لَهُ ونَصِيحَةً لِعِبَادِهِ، فَالْإِسْلَامُ عِنْدَ أَهْلِهِ عَظِيمٌ شَأْنُهُ، مَعْرُوفٌ سَبِيلُهُ، لِحُقُوقِهِ مُتَفَقِّدُونَ، ولَهُ مُتَعاهِدُونَ، يَعْرِفُونَهُ ويُعْرَفُونَ بِهِ، بِالِاجْتِهَادِ بِالنِّيَّةِ، وَالِاقْتِصَادِ بِالسُّنَّةِ، لَا يَبْطُرُهُمْ عَنْهُ رَخَاءٌ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا أصَابَهُمْ، وَلَا يُضَيِّعُونَهُ لِشِدَّةِ بَلَاءٍ نَزَلَ بِهِمْ، ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ جَاءَهُمْ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ، أَيْقَنَتْ نُفُوسُهُمْ، واطْمَأَنَّتْ بِهِ قُلُوبُهُمْ، يَسِيرُونَ مِنْهُ عَلَى أعْلَامِ نَبِيِّهِ، وَسُبِلٍ واضِحَةٍ. حُكْمٌ فَرَغَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ، لَا تَلْتَبِسُ بِهِ الْأهْوَاءُ، وَلَا تَزِيغُ بِهِ الْقُلُوبُ، عَهِدَ عَهْدَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَى عِبَادِهِ، وَإِنَّمَا كَانَتْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةُ كَبَعْضِ الْأُمَمِ الَّتِي مَضَتْ قَبْلَهَا جَاءَهَا نَذِيرٌ مِنْهَا، ودَعَاها بِمَا يُحْيِيهَا، وَنَصَحَ لَهَا، وَجَهَدَ وَأَدَّى الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ، فاسْتَجَابَ لَهُ مُسْتَجِيبُونَ، وكَذَّبَ بِهِ مُكَذِّبُونَ، فَقَاتَلَ مَنْ كَذَّبَهُ بِمَنِ اسْتَجَابَ لَهُ. حَتَّى أحَلَّ حَلَالَ اللَّهِ، وَحَرَّمَ حَرَامَهُ، وَعَمِلَ بِطَاعَتِهِ، ثُمَّ نَزَلَ بِهَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ مَوْعُودُ اللَّهِ، الَّذِي وَعَدَ مِنْ وُقُوعِ الْفِتْنَةِ، يُفَارِقُ رِجالٌ عَلَيْهِ رِجالًا، وَيُوالِي ⦗ص: 148⦘ رِجالٌ عَلَيْهِ رِجالًا. فَمَنْ أرَادَ أَنْ يُسَائِلَنَا عَنْ أَمْرِنَا وَرَأْيِنَا فَإِنَّا قَوْمٌ اللَّهُ رَبُّنَا، وَالْإِسْلَامُ دِينُنَا، وَالْقُرْآنُ إِمَامُنَا، وَمُحَمَّدٌ نَبِيُّنا، إِلَيْهِ نَسْنُدُ، ونُضِيفُ أَمْرَنَا إِلَى اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ، ونَرْضَى مِنْ أَئِمَّتِنَا بِأَبِي بَكْرٍ وعُمَرَ، ونَرْضَى أَنْ يُطَاعَا ونَسْخَطُ أَنْ يُعْصَيَا، ونُعَادِي لَهُمَا مَنْ عادَاهُمَا، ونُرْجِي مِنْهُمْ أَهْلَ الْفُرْقَةِ الْأُوَلَ. ونُجَاهِدُ فِي أَبِي بَكْرٍ وعُمَرَ الْوِلَايَةَ، فَإِنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ وعُمَرَ لمْ تَقْتَتِلْ فيهِمَا الْأُمَّةُ، وَلَمْ تَخْتَلِفْ فيهِمَا، وَلَمْ يُشَكَّ فِي أَمْرِهِمَا، وَإِنَّمَا الْإِرْجَاءُ مِمَّنْ عَابَ الرِّجَالَ، وَلَمْ يَشْهَدْهُ، ثُمَّ عَابَ عَلَيْنَا الْإِرْجَاءَ مِنَ الْأُمَّةِ وقَالَ مَتَى كَانَ الْإِرْجَاءُ. كَانَ عَلَى عَهْدِ مُوسَى نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ، إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ فِرْعَونُ {مَا بَالُ الْقُرُونِ الْأُولَى} طَهَ: قَالَ مُوسَى وَهُوَ يَنْزِلُ عَلَيْهِ الْوَحْيُ: حَتَّى قَالَ: {عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنْسَى} [طه: 52] طَهَ:. فَلَمْ يُعَنَّفْ بِمِثْلِ حُجَّةِ مُوسَى، وَمِمَّنْ نُعَادِي فِيهِمْ، شَبِيبَةٌ مُتَمَنِّيَةٌ ظَهَرُوا بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ، وأعْلَنُوا الْفِرْيَةَ عَلَى بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ، وعَلَى اللَّهِ، لَا يُفَارِقُونَ النَّاسَ بِبَصَرٍ نَافِذٍ، وَلَا عَقْلٍ بَالِغٍ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ، يَنْقُمُونَ الْمَعْصِيَةَ عَلَى مَنْ عَمِلَهَا، ويَعْمَلُونَ بِهَا. إِذَا ظَهَرُوا بِهَا يَنْصُرونَ فِتْنَتَها وَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ الْمَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا، اتَّخَذُوا أَهْلَ بَيْتٍ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ إِمَامًا، وقَلَّدُوهُمْ دِينَهُمْ، يَتْلُونَ عَلَى حُبِّهِمْ ويُفَارِقُونَ عَلَى بُغْضِهِمْ، جُفَاةٌ عَلَى الْقُرْآنِ، أتْبَاعُ الْكُهَّانِ، يَرْجُونَ دَوْلَةً تَكُونُ فِي بَعْثٍ يَكُونُ قَبْلَ السَّاعَةِ، أوْ قَبْلَ قِيَامِ السَّاعَةِ، حَرَّفُوا كِتَابَ اللَّهِ، وارْتَشَوْا فِي الْحُكْمِ، وسَعَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا، وَاللَّهِ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ، وفَتَحُوا أَبْوَابًا كَانَ اللَّهُ سَدَّهَا، وسَدُّوا أَبْوابًا كَانَ اللَّهُ فَتَحَهَا، وَمِنْ خُصُومَةِ هَذِهِ الشَّبِيبَةِ الَّتِي أَدْرَكْنَا، أَنْ يَقُولُوا: هُدِينَا بِوَحْيٍ ضَلَّ عَنْهُ النَّاسُ، وَعِلْمٍ خَفِيَ، ويَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ كَتَمَ تِسْعَةَ أَعْشَارِ الْقُرْآنِ. وَلَوْ كَانَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ كاتِمًا شَيْئًا مِمَّا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ، لَكَتَمَ شَأْنَ امْرَأَةِ زَيْدٍ {إِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ} [الأحزاب: 37] الْأَحْزَابُ: وَقَوْلَهُ {لِمَ تُحَرِّمْ مَا أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ} [التحريم: 1] التَّحْرِيمُ وَقَوْلَهُ {لَقَدْ كِدْتَ تَرْكَنَ إِلَيْهِمْ شَيْئًا قَلِيلًا} [الإسراء: 74] الْإِسْرَاءُ: فَهَذَا أَمْرُنَا ورَأْيُنَا، وَنَدْعُو إِلَى اللَّهِ مَنْ أَجَابَنَا، ونُجِيبُ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ دَعَانَا، لَا نَأْلُو فِيهِ عَنْ طَاعَةِ رَبِّنَا، وأدَاءِ الْحَقِّ الَّذِي ⦗ص: 149⦘ عَلَيْنَا، ونُذَكِّرُ بِهِ قَوْمَنَا وَمَنْ سَأَلَنَا مِنْ أَئِمَّتِنَا، فَيَسْتَحِلُّونَ بَعْدَهُ دِمَاءَنَا، أوْ يُعْرِضُوا دِمَاءَهُمْ لَنَا. فَالنَّاسُ مَجْمُوعُونَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ فِي مَوْطِنِ صِدْقٍ، ويَوْمَ يَكُونُ الْحَقُّ للَّهِ، ويَبْرَأُ فِيهِ الْبَائِعُ مِنَ الْمَبْيُوعِ، وَيَدْعُو الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بِالثُّبُورِ، فادَّخِرُوا مِنْ صَالِحِ الْحُجَجِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ لَا يَكُونُ يَظْفَرُ بِحُجَّتِهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا، لَمْ يَظْفَرْ بِهَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ، كِتَابٌ كَتَبْتُهُ نَصِيحَةً لِمَنْ قَبْلَهُ، وَحُجَّةً عَلَى مَنْ تَرَكَهُ، وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ وَالْحَمْدُ للَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ "
records.isnad_en: Ibrāhīm b. ʿUyayna narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ayman narrated to us. He said:
records.matn_en: Al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad b. al-Ḥanafiyya used to command that I read this letter to the people: “To proceed: We counsel you to fear God, and urge you to His command; we are pleased for you with obedience to Him, and displeased for you with disobedience to Him. God sent down the Book with His knowledge and made it firm, and made it detailed, and made it mighty, and protected it from falsehood coming to it from before it or from behind it; He struck its parables, made clear its lessons, and made it a criterion (furqān) against evil, a light from darkness, sight from blindness, and guidance from error. Then the favor was completed, worship was perfected, the charge was preserved, the sunna ran its course and the admonition went forth, the covenant was bound, and obedience was made incumbent. So it is the firm rope of God and the most trustworthy handhold that has no breaking; by it the earlier ones advanced and by it the later ones attained: a book whose judgment He Himself took charge of, which He approved for Himself and made obligatory upon His servants. Whoever preserves it, it conveys him to what is beyond it; and whoever neglects it, nothing else will be accepted from him. To proceed: God, blessed and exalted, sent down prophethood upon Muḥammad and sent him with the message, a mercy to all people, while people were then in the darkness of the Jāhiliyya and its misguidance, worshipping its idols and casting lots with its divining arrows; from them they took counsel in their affairs, and by them they made lawful what they made lawful and forbade what they forbade; their religion was innovation and their call was fabrication. So God, mighty and majestic, sent Muḥammad ﷺ with the truth, as a mercy from Him to you and a favor He bestowed upon you; he gave you glad tidings and warned you, [reminding you of] the mention of the nations before you, and the Book recounted the story of their affair: how their messengers gave them sincere counsel, how they denied them and turned away from them, and how was God’s punishment of them. So God admonished you with the exemplary punishment of those before you and commanded you to emulate their righteous deeds. Muḥammad conveyed the message, gave sincere counsel to the community, acted in obedience, and fought the enemy; God exalted His cause through him, made His light manifest through him, and perfected His word through him. He chose for him peoples who knew the right of God and acknowledged it, and who gave up their blood and wealth for Him. Among them were those who abandoned their home and kin for God, mighty and majestic, and among them were those who sheltered and aided; they consoled him with their own selves and shared with him. They did not prefer their own lives to his life. Through them God strengthened the religion, and truth crushed [p. 147] falsehood; the call of the false deities (ṭawāghīt) was nullified, the divining arrows were broken, the worship of idols was abandoned, the caller to God was answered and the religion of God became manifest. People came to know the command of God, mighty and majestic, acknowledged God’s decree, testified to the truth, said ‘There is no god but God; Muḥammad is the Messenger of God,’ and performed the obligations of God, mighty and majestic. And God gave His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ and those who responded to him, in recompense, reward, victory, promise and authority; He established for them their religion that He approved and exchanged for them, after their fear, security. Then, when God had firmly established the prohibition of disobedience to Him, the call had become pure, and Islam had been made secure for its people, He legislated the laws of the religion and decreed its obligations, set a mark of the religion that the people of Islam know, set the limits (ḥudūd), made the sacred rites inviolable, and taught the rites of pilgrimage; the sunna passed on, He called the sinner to repent, called to emigration, and opened the door of repentance, as a proof for Himself and good counsel for His servants. Islam among its people is great in standing and its path is known; they watch over its rights and attend to it; they know it and are known by it, with striving in intention and moderation in the sunna. No ease of the world that comes upon them makes them insolent toward it, and they do not neglect it because of severe affliction that befalls them. That is because God’s command came to them; their souls became certain and their hearts were at ease with it; they proceed by it on the signposts of His Prophet and clear paths. A judgment God has finished with, by which desires are not confused and hearts do not swerve; a covenant God made with His servants. This community was only like some of the nations that passed before it: a warner came to it from among itself, and called it to what gives it life, gave it sincere counsel, strove and discharged what was upon him of the truth; some responded to him and some denied him, and he fought those who denied him with those who responded to him, until he made lawful what God made lawful, forbade what He forbade, and acted in obedience to Him. Then there came upon this community what God had promised of the occurrence of tribulation (fitna): men separate from men over it, and men [p. 148] ally with men over it. So whoever wishes to ask us about our affair and our view: we are a people whose Lord is God, whose religion is Islam, whose leader (imām) is the Qurʾān, and whose Prophet is Muḥammad; to him we trace back [our affair], and we refer our affair to God and His Messenger. Of our leaders we are content with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; we are pleased that they be obeyed and displeased that they be disobeyed, and we are hostile, on their behalf, to whoever is hostile to them; and we defer judgment (nurjī) concerning the people of the first division. And we strive for the allegiance (wilāya) of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, for the community did not fight over Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, nor differ about them, nor was there doubt about their affair. Deferral (irjāʾ) is only [for the case of] those who found fault with the men without having witnessed it, and then found fault with us for deferral from the community and said: When was there deferral? It was in the time of Moses, the prophet of God, when Pharaoh said to him “What of the former generations?” [Q. 20:51]; Moses said, while revelation was coming down upon him, until He said: “Their knowledge is with my Lord in a record; my Lord neither errs nor forgets” [Q. 20:52]. So he was not reproached with the like of Moses’ proof. And among those we are hostile to are a wishful youth (shabība mutamanniya) who have appeared with the Book of God, and have publicly spread slander against the Banū Umayya and against God; they do not part from the people with penetrating insight or mature reason in Islam. They resent disobedience in those who commit it, and they commit it themselves. When they gain the upper hand through it, they support its tribulation and do not know the way out of it. They have taken a household (ahl bayt) of the Arabs as imām and followed them blindly in their religion; they follow in love of them and part ways in hatred of them; coarse toward the Qurʾān, followers of soothsayers; they hope for a dominion to come with a resurrection (baʿth) that will occur before the Hour, or before the rising of the Hour. They distorted the Book of God, took bribes in judgment, and strove in the land to spread corruption—and God does not love the corrupters; they opened doors that God had closed, and closed doors that God had opened. And part of the disputation of this youth whom we have met is that they say: We have been guided by a revelation from which the people have gone astray, and by knowledge that was hidden; and they claim that the Prophet of God concealed nine-tenths of the Qurʾān. Yet if the Prophet of God had been concealing anything of what God sent down, he would have concealed the matter of Zayd’s wife, “when you said to him on whom God had bestowed favor” [Q. 33:37] (al-Aḥzāb), and His saying “Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?” [Q. 66:1] (al-Taḥrīm), and His saying “You were about to incline to them a little” [Q. 17:74] (al-Isrāʾ). This, then, is our affair and our view. We call to God whoever responds to us, and respond to Him whoever calls us, not falling short in it of obedience to our Lord and of discharging the right [p. 149] that is upon us; and we remind our people of it, and whoever asks us among our leaders, [but] after it they deem our blood lawful—or expose their own blood to us. People will be gathered before their Lord in a station of truth, on a day when the truth belongs to God, when the seller disowns what is sold, and when man calls upon himself for destruction. So store up righteous proofs with God, for whoever does not succeed with his proof in this world will not succeed with it in the Hereafter. [This is] a letter I have written as sincere counsel for whoever receives it and a proof against whoever abandons it. Peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”
translator_notes: This narration is a letter attributed to al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad b. al-Ḥanafiyya, not a ḥadīth of the Prophet; it is the epistle on deferral (irjāʾ). ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ayman reports that al-Ḥasan commanded him to read it to the people. The letter contains many rare or obscure expressions (for example the verb in ‘Islam … for its people’, ‘shabība mutamanniya’, and the closing sentences on ‘deeming blood lawful’), and the rendering is tentative in these places; the sūra names Ṭā-Hā, al-Aḥzāb, al-Taḥrīm and al-Isrāʾ are added after the verses in the source, and the verse reference for Q. 20:51 is supplied here.

groups.title_en: Chapter: A believer does not commit treacherous assassination (fatk)

records.isnad_ar: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ لِلزُّبَيْرِ أَلَا أَقْتُلُ لَكَ عَلِيًّا قَالَ: كَيْفَ تَقْتُلُهُ؟ قَالَ: أَغْتَالُهُ، فَقَالَ: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ: «الْإِيمَانُ قَيَّدَ الْفَتْكَ لَا يَفْتِكُ مُؤْمِنٌ»
records.isnad_en: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from al-Ḥasan, that a man said to al-Zubayr:
records.matn_en: Shall I kill ʿAlī for you? He said: How would you kill him? He said: I would assassinate him. He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Faith has shackled treachery (fatk); a believer does not commit treacherous assassination.”
translator_notes: al-Ḥasan reports an event involving al-Zubayr without naming his source; the man who makes the offer is not named.
